mobile-app: Mobile app Overview The Direct Home Service mobile app is the field companion to the web platform. It is built for service providers — technicians, crew leads, and owners — who need to run their day from a phone or tablet: check the schedule, work jobs, capture estimates and invoices, track time, manage the client list and catalog, and stay in touch with clients and the office. With the mobile app you can: See your day at a glance on the Home dashboard, with your key numbers and upcoming work. Work jobs end to end — travel with directions, run a work timer, add services and products, complete a checklist, and bill the client. Schedule and manage appointments , then convert them into estimates, jobs, or invoices. Create and send estimates and invoices , take payments, and track what is owed. Manage clients, properties, and your catalog of services and products. Track time with automatic and manual timesheet entries. Message clients and your team , and ask the built-in AI Assistant in English or Spanish. Note: The app adapts to your device — a compact bottom navigation bar on phones (built around a central Work Hub) and a fuller navigation rail on tablets. On the Solo plan , crew-related fields are hidden throughout. Getting Started Welcome to the Direct Home Service mobile app — your field companion for running jobs, scheduling, estimates, invoices, and time tracking from your phone or tablet. This article walks you through signing in and finding your way around. Sign in Open the app. Enter the email and password for your DHS account (the same login you use on the web). Tap Sign In . Your session is remembered, so you won't need to sign in every time. If your details are wrong or your account is disabled, you'll see an error — contact your administrator if you can't get in. New here? First-time users see a short intro and, after signing in, a quick welcome tour. The bottom navigation bar On a phone, five slots are always visible: Home — your dashboard and daily summary (a badge appears when you have unread alerts). Scheduler — the calendar of your appointments and jobs. Work Hub — the center button; opens Jobs, Appointments, and Estimates. AI — the AI Assistant. More — Clients, Invoices, Timesheets, Services, Products, Settings, Help and Support and sign-out. The active section is highlighted. Tapping a slot switches to it and remembers where you left off. The Work Hub The raised center button is the Work Hub — your day-to-day work lives here. Tap it and choose: Jobs — the work you're doing. Appointments — scheduled visits. Estimates — quotes for clients. The More menu Tap More to reach: Clients Invoices Timesheets Services and Products Settings Help & Support (opens the online help center) The Log Out button is located at the bottom of the screen. Your Account & Profile This article covers signing in, updating your profile, changing your password and language, getting help, and signing out. Create an account New service providers can sign up from the Sign Up link on the Sign In screen. It's a two-step form: Personal Information — choose your Plan (Standard or Solo), then enter your name, email, phone, and a password. Passwords must be at least 10 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character. Company Info — enter your company name, address, zip, time zone, and (optionally) website and up to three service categories. Tap Sign Up to finish. Your profile To view and edit your profile, tap your name/avatar at the top of the Home dashboard to open My Profile . Here you can: Update your profile picture ( Upload Image — 2 MB max; or Remove ). Edit your First Name , Last Name , Email , and Phone . View your Role and Time Zone . Tap Apply Changes to save. You'll see "Your profile has been successfully updated." Change your password On the My Profile screen, scroll to Change Password : Enter your Current Password . Enter and confirm a New Password (same strength rules as sign-up). Tap Change Password . Change your language On My Profile , under Language , choose English or Español . The app switches immediately. Tip: The AI Assistant also understands both languages — just type in whichever you prefer. Help & Support Tap More > Help & Support to open the online help center in your browser. Sign out Tap More , scroll to the bottom, and tap Log Out , then confirm. You'll return to the Sign In screen. Home Dashboard The Home dashboard is your starting point each day — a quick summary of your numbers, your jobs, and your open estimates and invoices. This article explains what's on it. Home is the first screen after signing in and the leftmost slot on the navigation bar. Pull down to refresh it at any time. Tap your name/avatar at the top to open My Profile , and tap the bell icon to see notifications. Overview cards Four cards summarize your business at a glance: Total Jobs Total Real Profit Pending Invoices (with a View shortcut) Total Potential Profit Each card shows a trend chip — green (up) or red (down) versus the previous period, or grey when there's no change. Jobs The Jobs section lists your work with Upcoming and Today tabs. Each card shows the job name, status, crew, and scheduled date/time — tap it to open the job. Use View all to jump to the full Jobs list, or Add Job to create one. Open estimates and invoices Open Estimates — your active quotes, each with its status, crew, and total. Tap View all . Open Invoices — unpaid bills, each with its number, job, status, and total. Tap View all . Tap any card to open that record. The work timer If you have a timer running on a job or appointment, a timer bar appears on the dashboard with a View Job shortcut and a stop control, so you can manage your active time from anywhere. Notifications A red dot on the bell icon means you have unread alerts. Tap it to open the notifications list, where you can read them and tap any item to jump straight to the related job, estimate, invoice, or appointment. Scheduler (Calendar) The Scheduler is your calendar of appointments and jobs. This article covers switching views, moving through dates, filtering by crew (Standard and Team Plans only), and creating work from the calendar. Open the Scheduler tab (bottom navigation) to see your appointments and jobs laid out by time, so you can plan your route and your day. Pull down to refresh. Switch calendar views Use the tabs at the top to change the view: Day — one day's timeline. Week — a week strip with the day's events. Month — a full month grid; days with events show colored dots and a "+N" when there are several. List — a simple list of the selected day's events. Move through dates Tap Today to jump back to the current day. Use the back / forward arrows to step by day, week, or month (depending on your view). Tap the date label to open a date picker and jump to any day. Filter by crew Use the crew dropdown to focus on one crew's schedule, or choose All Crews to see everything. (Standard and Team Plans only) Open a job or appointment Tap any event on the calendar to open it — appointments open the appointment detail, jobs open the job detail. In List view, each row shows the type (Appointment or Job), start/end times, and crew. Create from the calendar Tap an empty time slot to open the Create New Event sheet, then choose: New Job — creates a scheduled job at that time. New Appointment — creates a scheduled appointment at that time. The create form opens pre-filled with the date and time you tapped. Jobs Jobs are the work you schedule, track, and bill from your phone. This article covers creating a job, running the work timer, adding services and products, completing the job, and billing your client. A job is scheduled work assigned to a crew for a client's property. From a job you can travel to the site with directions, log your hours, record the services and products used, complete a checklist, and turn it all into an invoice — without leaving the app. Note: On the Solo plan , the Crew field is hidden throughout Jobs (a single crew is used automatically). Open the Jobs list Tap the Work Hub (the center button of the bottom navigation bar) and choose Jobs . From here you can: Search by keyword, or tap the filter icon to show only certain statuses. Tap any job card to open it. Tap + (top right) to create a new job. Each card shows the job name, client, scheduled date/time, crew, and a colored status pill. Create a job On the Jobs list, tap + . Step 1 of 2 – Job Details: choose the Client , Property , and Crew . Optionally pick a Checklist and turn on Priority Job . Tap Next Step . Step 2 of 2 – Start & End Dates: pick the start date and time, then the end date and time. Turn on Override Business Hours to schedule outside normal hours, or Is Locked to prevent schedule changes. Tap Add Job . Tip: If the client doesn't exist in your account yet, you can add them directly from the Clients dropdown by selecting Quick Add → New Client . Track your time (En Route, Work, Stop) Open a job and use the timer bar . The timer logs your hours and moves the job's status automatically: En Route – opens directions and your ETA, then starts travel time and sets the job to En Route . Start Work Time – begins job time and sets the job to Started . Start Office Time / Job Prep Time – log those hours separately. Stop – ends the running timer. Note: The timer is hidden once a job is Completed or Canceled . Add services and products In the job's Services or Products section, tap + to pick from your existing items — or use Quick Add to create a new one. Services have editable Time (hours/minutes) and Rate . Products have editable Quantity and Price . Each item shows a running Total . After editing a value, tap Apply Changes to save. Update the status Open the job and tap the Status pill to choose a new status (Draft, Scheduled, Pending, Confirmed, En Route, Arrived, Started, Paused, Completed, or Canceled). Note: Choosing Paused stops the timer. Choosing Completed or Canceled asks you to confirm first. Complete a job Set the status to Completed . If the job has a checklist , the Complete Job screen opens first — fill in any required items, then tap Complete Job . If there's no checklist, just confirm. Completing a job stops any running timer. Bill your client and create an invoice In the job's Bill section, review the Subtotal , add Tax , and enter any Discount or Required Deposit . Tap Apply Changes . Tap More > Create Invoice to generate an invoice from the job and open it. Note: Create Invoice is only available once the job has at least one service or product. Reschedule or delete a job Reschedule: open the job, tap More > Reschedule , and pick new start/end dates. Delete: use the ⋮ menu on the job card (or More on the detail screen) and confirm. Deleting a job is permanent. Appointments Appointments are scheduled visits with a client — a quote visit, an inspection, or any on-site meeting. This article covers creating an appointment, scheduling it, running the visit timer, and turning it into an estimate, job, or invoice. An appointment ties a client and property to a date and time, optionally with a crew and the services you expect to perform. From an appointment you can log time on site, then convert the visit into an estimate , job , or invoice once it's complete. Note: On the Solo plan , the Crew field is hidden throughout. Open the Appointments list Tap the Work Hub (center button) and choose Appointments . Use the two tabs — Active and Archived . Search by keyword, or tap the filter icon to filter by status. Tap + (top right) to create one. Tap any card to open it. Each card shows the appointment name, client, Scheduled for date/time (with a "(Today)" / "(Tomorrow)" hint), crew, and a colored status pill. Create an appointment Tap + on the Appointments list. Step 1 – Enter Details: enter the Client , Property , and Crew (Standard and Team Plans only) . Tap Next . Step 2 – Schedule & Review: set the date, time, and duration (see below), optionally add services, review the summary, and tap Submit . Tip: Not ready to schedule? Tap Save as Draft on step 2 to save the appointment as a Draft and finish it later. Schedule (date, time, duration) On the schedule step: Tap Select Date and pick a day. Unavailable days are greyed out; if you need one anyway, turn on Override to ignore business hours. Tap Select Time and choose from the Available times . If the day has none, you'll see "No available time slots." Choose a Duration — 30 minutes, 1 hour, 1.5 hours, 2 hours, or Custom (enter the minutes). You can also turn on High Priority or Callback (a callback links the visit to an existing job). Run the visit timer Open an appointment (unless it's Completed or Canceled) and use the timer : En Route starts travel time and sets the status to En Route . Start Work starts job time and sets the status to Started . Stop ends the running timer. Logged time appears in the Visits section of the appointment. Update the status Tap the Status pill to change it. Appointments move through: Draft, Scheduled, Pending, Confirmed, En Route, Arrived, Started, Completed, Canceled, and No Show. Note: Choosing Completed or Canceled asks you to confirm first. Convert to an estimate, job, or invoice Open the appointment and go to the Related Records tab. Once the appointment is Completed , you can: Convert to Estimate — creates an estimate from the visit. Convert to Job — schedules a job from the visit. Add Invoice — bills the visit (requires that the appointment has services). Note: These buttons are disabled until the appointment status is Completed . Send the appointment to your client From the appointment details section, open the More menu and select Send to Client . Choose Email , SMS , or both, edit the subject and message, and click Send to Client . Use Preview to see the message first. Note: Sending is available only once the appointment is scheduled and has a crew, and its status isn't Draft or Completed. Reschedule, archive, or delete Reschedule: open the appointment, tap More > Reschedule , and pick a new date/time. Set as Priority: toggle it from the More menu. Archive: from the card's ⋮ menu or More , tap Archive and confirm. Archived appointments move to the Archived tab. Restore / Delete: on the Archived tab, use the card's ⋮ menu to Restore or permanently Delete . Estimates An estimate is the quote you send a client before doing the work. This article covers creating an estimate, adding services and products, sending it for approval, and converting an approved estimate into a job. An estimate lists the services and products you propose, with pricing, and can be sent to the client to review, comment on, or approve with a signature. Estimates move through four statuses: Draft , Ready for Review , Changes Requested , and Approved . Note: Once an estimate is Approved or Ready for Review , its line items and totals are locked from editing. On the Solo plan , the Crew field is hidden. Open the Estimates list Tap the Work Hub (center button) and choose Estimates . Search by keyword, or tap the filter icon to filter by status. Tap + (top right) to create one. Tap any card to open it. Each card shows the estimate name, client, date created, crew, status , and total . Create an estimate Tap + on the Estimates list. Step 1 – Estimate Details: enter the Client , Property , and Crew (Standard and Team Plans only) . Tap Next Step . Step 2 – Quick Add: add the services and products for the quote (see below). Tap Add Estimate . Tip: If a client or property doesn't exist yet, use the New Client / Property button inside the picker to add it without leaving the form. Add services and products In the Services and Products sections, tap + to pick an existing item — or use Quick Add to create a new one on the spot. Services have editable Time (hours/minutes) and Rate . Products have editable Quantity and Price . Each line shows a running Total . After changing a value, tap Apply Changes . Adjust the bill (tax, discount, deposit) Open the estimate and scroll to the Bill section: Tax — tap to pick a tax rate (or remove it). Discount — enter an amount. Required Deposit — enter an amount you want up front. The Total updates automatically. Tap Apply Changes to save. You can also add Comments to Client that appear on the estimate. Send the estimate to your client On the estimate, tap Submit Estimate . Choose Email , SMS , or both, and edit the subject and message. Tap Preview to review, then Send estimate . When you send the estimate, its status changes to Ready for Review . The client receives a link to view and approve it. When they approve and sign, the estimate shows an Approved by block with their signature and the date. Approve and convert to a job Once an estimate is Approved , open it and tap Convert to Job : Pick the Start Date and time. Pick the End Date and time. Tap Convert to Job . A job is created from the estimate's services and products. To edit an approved estimate first, tap Edit Estimate (this moves it back to Changes Requested ). Duplicate or delete From an estimate card's ⋮ menu (or the estimate's overview menu): Duplicate — creates a copy you can adjust for another client or property. Delete — removes the estimate (confirmation required). Note: You cannot delete or duplicate estimates that are currently marked as Approved or Ready for Review . Invoices An invoice is the bill you send a client for completed work. This article covers creating an invoice, sending it, recording payments, and tracking what's still owed. An invoice lists the services and products delivered, with pricing and totals, and tracks how much the client has paid. Invoices move through four statuses: Draft , Sent , Viewed , and Paid . Once an invoice is Paid , it becomes a read-only receipt. Open the Invoices list Tap More (bottom navigation) and choose Invoices . Search by keyword, or tap the filter icon to filter by status. Tap + (top right) to create one. Invoices are grouped by job — tap Job Details on a group header to open its job. Tap any invoice to open it. Each invoice shows its number , status , and total . Create an invoice Tap + on the Invoices list. Step 1 – Details: optionally add invoice details, then choose the Client , Property , and Job . Set the Issue Date and Due Date . Tap Next Step . Step 2 – Quick Add: add or confirm the services and products to bill. Tap Add Invoice . Tip: Selecting a Job automatically pulls that job's services and products into the invoice. Adjust the bill (tax, discount, deposit) Open the invoice's Overview tab and scroll to the Bill section: Tax — tap to pick a tax rate (or remove it). Discount and Required Deposit — enter amounts. The Total updates automatically. Tap Apply Changes to save. Send the invoice to your client On the invoice, tap Send Invoice . Choose Email , SMS , or both, and edit the subject and message. Tap Preview to review, then Send invoice . The client receives a link to view the invoice, which moves the status to Sent (and Viewed once they open it). Record a payment Open the invoice and go to the Payments tab. Tap + to add a payment. Enter the Date , Type (Credit Card, Bank Transfer, Check, Cash, Payment Processor, or Other), Status , and Amount . Add a reference or note if you like. Tap Add Payment . Tip: If there's a balance owed, the amount field pre-fills with the remaining balance and the status defaults to Completed . Track payments and the balance due The Payments tab shows a summary — Total , Required Deposit , and Remaining — plus a Payments History list. Use each payment's ⋮ menu to Edit or Delete it. Mark as paid or delete Mark as paid: tap the Status pill and choose Paid . The invoice becomes a read-only receipt. Delete: from the invoice's More menu (or the list card's ⋮ ), tap Delete and confirm. Clients Clients are the customers you do business with. This article covers finding clients, adding them, managing their properties, and viewing their related work. A client can be a homeowner (Residential) or a company (Business). Each client can have multiple properties, and all their appointments, estimates, jobs, and invoices are linked to their account. Open the Clients list Tap More > Clients . Switch between Active and Archived tabs. Search by name, or tap the filter icon to filter by city, state, property type, or tags. Tap + to add a client, or tap any row to open it. Each row shows the client's name, type, phone, email, and tags. Add a client Tap + on the Clients list. Step 1 – Client Info: enter the required First Name , Last Name , Phone , and Email . Optionally add a company name, website, attachments and tags. Step 2 – Property & Review: input the initial property details for the client (type, address, state, city, zip, and timezone), as well as billing information; an optional property image may be uploaded. Finally, review the summary and tap Add client . Tip: You can turn on Billing address same as property to copy the address automatically. Existing client check: as you enter the email or phone in Step 1, the app checks whether a client already exists with those details. If it finds a match, it prompts you so you don't create a duplicate — and lets you Send invite to give that client portal access ("Invite sent successfully," or "Invite already sent" if one is still pending). Client details Open a client to see their record, organized in tabs: Properties — all of the client's properties. Appointments , Estimates , and Job & Invoices — everything linked to that client. From here you can also start a new job, estimate, or invoice with the client pre-filled, using the More menu. Manage properties On the Properties tab: Tap + New Property to add one. Tap a property to view it; use Show map to see its location. Each property card shows the address, type, and image. Notes and attachments Notes and attachments exist in two places — make sure you're in the right one: Client-level: from the client's page, tap More → Client Details , then use the Notes or Attachments tab. Property-level: from the client's page, tap a property card to open it, then use its own Notes or Attachments tab. Message a client Tap Chat (or Start a Conversation from the list ⋮ menu) to open the Inbox conversation with that client. Archive and restore Use the row's ⋮ menu: Archive — hides the client from active views but keeps all their history. Restore — brings an archived client back. Note: Archiving never deletes a client's appointments, estimates, jobs, or invoices. Services & Products Services and products are the items you add to jobs, estimates, and invoices. A service is labor you charge by the hour; a product is a physical item you sell with a cost, markup, and (optionally) inventory tracking. This article covers finding, creating, editing, and archiving both. Your catalog has two separate lists — Services and Products — each with its own Active and Archived tabs. Items you create here become available to add to jobs, estimates, and invoices. An item is either Active or Archived , and can be marked Taxable and shown on the client portal. Note: When you add a product to a job, estimate, or invoice, any product that's out of stock appears disabled and can't be selected until it's back in stock. Open Services and Products Both live under the More tab (bottom navigation): Tap More > Services to open the Services list. Tap More > Products to open the Products list. On each list you can search , tap the filter icon to narrow results, switch between Active and Archived , and tap + to create a new item. Tap any row to open its detail. A service row shows: name, SKU, Rate (cost per hour), whether it's Taxable , In Use , shown on the Client Portal , plus tags and groups. A product row shows: image, name, SKU, Cost , Markup % , Item Price , whether it's Taxable and In Use , plus tags and groups. Create a service On the Services list, tap + . Step 1 – Enter Details: fill in the required fields: SKU (required) Name (required) Cost Per Hour (required) Optionally add a Description and Tags . Taxable is on by default; Show on client portal is off by default. Tap Next . Step 2 – Attachments (optional): upload files by category — Specifications, Manual, Installation, Safety, or Other (PNG, PDF, or JPG). Tap Submit . You'll see "Service Item successfully created" and the item appears in your list. Create a product On the Products list, tap + . Fill in the required fields: SKU (required) Name (required) Cost (required) Enter a Markup % — the Item Price is calculated automatically as cost plus markup. Optionally add a product image (JPEG/PNG/WEBP, up to 4 MB), description , tags , and choose a Vendor , Manufacturer . Set inventory details if you track stock: Unit of Measure , Quantity On Hand , Re-Order Quantity , and Location . To turn tracking off, enable Disable Inventory Tracking . Taxable is on by default. Tap Submit . You'll see "Product successfully created." View or edit an item Tap a row to open its detail screen. A service detail has two tabs — Details (cost per hour, description, tags, groups, client-portal setting) and Attachments . A product detail shows its Item Price / Cost / Markup , catalog details (vendor, manufacturer, unit, groups, location), SKU , product image, Taxable and Active status, and inventory (tracking status, quantity on hand, re-order level). Tap Edit to change the item, then Update to save. You can also Archive the item directly from this screen. Note: In Use is set automatically — it shows "Yes" when the item is already used on a job, estimate, or invoice. Filter your catalog Tap the filter icon on either list to filter by: Tags Groups Taxable — show only tax-applicable items Client Portal — show only items visible in the client portal (Services only) Tap Filter to apply, or Reset to clear. The filter icon shows a badge with how many filters are active. Archive, restore, or delete Use a row's ⋮ menu (or the buttons on the detail screen): Archive — moves an active item to the Archived tab (confirmation required). Restore — brings an archived item back to Active. Delete — permanently removes an archived item (confirmation required). Note: You can only delete items that are archived first. Quick-add a vendor and manufacturer While creating or editing a product , you can add supporting records on the spot without leaving the form. Next to the Vendor and Manufacturer pickers, tap + Quick add : Vendor — a supplier you buy from. Captures a Name . Manufacturer — the maker of the product. Captures a Company Name . The new record is saved and selected in the product form automatically. Timesheets Timesheets track the hours you and your crew work. This article covers reviewing your hours, creating timesheets and time entries, and managing their status. A timesheet groups time entries for a user. Most entries are created automatically by the job and appointment timers (En Route, Job Time, Office Time, Job Prep), but you can also add and edit them by hand. Timesheets move through Draft , Pending , Approved , and Rejected . Note: Once a timesheet is Approved , its entries are locked from editing. On the Solo plan , the Crew field is hidden throughout Timesheets (a single crew is used automatically). Open Timesheets Tap More > Timesheets . Use search and the filter icon to find timesheets, and tap + to create one. Read the summary The Summary card at the top shows your totals: Total hours , Total en route hours , Total office time , and Total job time . Create a timesheet Tap + on the Timesheets screen. Pick a Date and, if you have a team, a User . Optionally add a Description . Tap Save . Add a time entry Open a timesheet and tap Add time . Pick the Date , then the Job or User . Choose the entry type — En route , Job time , Office hours , or Job prep . Set the From and To times and add a Description . Tap Save . Note: The end time must be after the start time and can't be in the future. Timesheet details Open a timesheet to see its Overview (date, crew, user) and its Time Entries . Each entry shows its job, type, and duration. Use an entry's ⋮ menu to view its description, edit, unlink, or delete it. Change the timesheet's status using the status chip at the top. Filter timesheets Tap the filter icon to filter by date range (with presets like This week, Last week, Last 30 days), user , and status . Inbox (Messaging) The Inbox is where you message clients and your team. This article covers starting conversations, switching between client and team chats, and sending messages. The Inbox keeps your conversations in one place. Each conversation is tied to a client and can be a direct chat or attached to a specific job, estimate, or invoice. Open the Inbox Tap More > Inbox . You'll see your conversations with the latest message preview and time. Use the Active and Archived tabs and the search field to find a chat, and tap one to open it. Start a new chat Tap + on the Inbox. Select a client (or use New client to add one). Type your message . Tap Send message . You can also start a conversation from a client's record — tap Chat (or Start a Conversation from the client list). Client vs. team conversations Inside a conversation, two tabs let you choose who you're talking to: Client — messages the client sees. Team — internal messages for your team only. Note: On the Solo plan, only the client conversation is shown. Send a message Type in the message bar and tap Send (the button reads Send to client or Send to team depending on the tab). You can attach files to a message. Archived conversations Archived chats appear under the Archived tab so your active list stays focused. AI Assistant The AI Assistant is a built-in helper you can talk to in plain language — by text, voice, or photo — to look things up and get answers about your business. This article covers how to use it on mobile. The AI Assistant understands everyday language in English and Spanish and replies right in the chat. It's on the AI slot of the bottom navigation bar. Open the AI Assistant Tap the AI button (sparkle icon) in the bottom navigation. You'll see a welcome screen with a few example prompts to get started. Ask by text Type your question or request in the input bar — for example, "Show my jobs for today" — and tap Send . The assistant replies in the chat and may show suggested follow-up actions below its answer. Ask by voice Tap the microphone button and speak your request. The assistant transcribes what you said, answers, and reads its reply back to you. Ask with a photo Tap the camera / image button to attach up to 5 photos (JPG, JPEG, or WEBP), then send. The assistant can analyze the image — useful for reading a note, identifying a product, or documenting a job site. If you don't add text, it will describe or analyze the image by default. Suggested prompts On the welcome screen, tap any of the example tiles to send it instantly: Show my jobs for today Create new estimate Show unpaid invoices Schedule appointment Tips Be specific — include names, dates, or numbers when you can. Use follow-ups — the assistant remembers the conversation, so you can say "which of those are unpaid?" without repeating yourself. Switch languages freely — write in English or Spanish; it adapts automatically. Double-check actions — confirm the assistant did what you intended, especially when it creates or changes a record. Quick Add Quick Add lets you create common records fast, with just the essential fields, from anywhere in the app. This article covers what you can quick-add and how it works. Quick Add is the fastest way to create a record without opening a full form. Every quick-add captures only the must-have fields and marks the record as incomplete, so you can finish the details later. Use Quick Add Tap the ⚡ Quick Add button in the bottom navigation. Choose what to create from the grid. Fill in the essential fields and tap Save . You'll get a confirmation like "New Client added using Quick Add," often with a View shortcut to open the record. Note: Records created via Quick Add show a small "finish setup" badge in their list until you complete the missing details. What you can create From the Quick Add grid you can create: Appointment Client Job Estimate Crew (hidden on Solo plan) User (hidden on Solo plan) Service item (a service or a product) Property Payment Inviting a client When you quick-add a client , as you enter their email or phone the app checks whether they already exist. You can Send invite to give them portal access — you'll see "Invite sent successfully," or "Invite already sent" if one is still pending. Quick-adds inside other forms You'll also find + Quick add buttons inside pickers throughout the app, so you never have to leave what you're doing. For example, while adding a product you can quick-add a Vendor (name), Manufacturer (company name), or Group (name and code) — and while scheduling a job you can quick-add a client, property, or crew on the spot. Notifications The app keeps you informed with push notifications and an in-app alerts list. This article covers where to find them and how they work. Notifications alert you to things that need attention — new job assignments, incoming messages, payment and invoice updates, timesheet approvals, and reminders. They arrive as push notifications on your device and also collect in an in-app Alerts list. See your notifications When you have unread alerts, a badge appears on the Home icon in the navigation bar. Open the dashboard and tap the bell icon to see the full list. Pull down to refresh, and scroll to load older ones. Each notification shows an icon for its type (job, estimate, invoice, appointment, timesheet, and so on), the time it arrived, and its message. Unread notifications are highlighted with a colored dot. Open a notification Tap a notification to mark it read and jump straight to the related record — for example, a job, estimate, invoice, or appointment. Mark as read Tap the mark-all-as-read button (open-envelope icon) at the top of the Alerts screen to clear all unread notifications at once. Tapping any single notification also marks just that one as read. Working Offline Basements, crawl spaces, rural properties, parking garages — plenty of the places you work have no signal. The app is built for that: it keeps a copy of your data on the device, so you can carry on working, and sends everything up when you're back on a connection. Getting set up The first time you sign in, the app downloads your data and shows Setting up your workspace . Let it finish before you head out somewhere without signal — that download is what makes offline work possible. After that, later passes just say Refreshing your data . If you go offline before it finished, the app tells you plainly: Setup incomplete — offline , and that "Some data hasn't finished downloading, so parts of the app may be unavailable offline." The sync indicator A small indicator tells you where you stand at any moment: It says It means Synced Everything is up to date, both ways. Syncing Data is moving — either coming down or going up. Offline No connection. You can keep working. Queued You have changes waiting to upload. Conflict Something needs your decision. See below. Tap it for the detail: what's still waiting to upload, and whether the app is pulling from the server or sending your changes. What happens to work you do offline Carry on as normal. Start jobs, run timers, add services and products, write notes, complete checklists, create clients — it's all saved on the device and marked Unsynced so you can see what hasn't gone up yet. You don't have to remember to send it: "Your queued changes will upload automatically when you reconnect." If an upload does fail, the app says Couldn't upload and offers Retry rather than losing the change. What needs a connection Two things can't work from a local copy: Attachments — photos and files. "Attachments require an internet connection." The AI Assistant — "The AI assistant needs an internet connection. Reconnect to ask a question." Worth knowing before you drive out: if you need a document from a client's record on site, open it while you still have signal. When two people changed the same thing If you edit a job offline and someone in the office edits the same job, the app can't know which one is right — so it stops rather than guessing. You'll see Sync paused — conflicts found and a Resolve conflicts button, telling you how many items "were changed both here and on the server." Resolving them is a short review, one record at a time. For each one, the app explains why it's a conflict: It was also changed on the server while you were offline. It was deleted on the server while you were offline — and keeping your version will restore it. A matching record already exists on the server, which usually means the same thing got created twice. Then you choose, with Your version and Server version shown side by side: Choice What it does Keep yours Your offline version wins. Keep server The office version wins and your change is dropped. Merge field-by-field Go through the differing fields and pick per field — for when you're both right about different things. Move through them with Next conflict and Previous , change your mind with Change resolution , and finish with Finish & resume sync . Syncing picks up where it left off. Two things to expect: leaving halfway asks "Discard your changes?" and warns that your selections will be lost, and a record that other pending changes depend on can't be deleted — "Deleting is off for this record — it's linked to other pending changes." Offline settings Under Settings you can control how much the app does offline. With everything on, it behaves as described above. Sync now — pull the latest changes without waiting. Greyed out with an explanation when you have no connection. Offline mode — turn it off and the app works purely online: nothing is read from or saved to the device, and syncing stops. Background sync & live updates — turn it off and the app stops syncing in the background and no longer picks up live changes from the server. You can't switch these off while you have unsynced work. The app blocks it: "You have unsynced changes. Connect to the internet so they can sync before turning this off." That's deliberate — it's what stops a setting change from throwing away a day in the field. Settings Settings is where you manage your business configuration from the app — your invoice numbering and tax rates, your working availability, and which notifications you receive. This article covers the Settings hub and its three areas: Business, Availability, and Notifications. Settings lives under the More tab, in the App & Support group. The Settings hub is a simple menu with three tiles — Business , Availability , and Notifications — each opening its own screen. Changes are saved per screen and take effect immediately once you tap Save . Open Settings Tap More (bottom navigation). Under App & Support , tap Settings . Choose Business , Availability , or Notifications . Business Settings Tap Settings > Business to manage your invoice numbering and tax rates. Invoice Number Counter — the number your next invoice will use. Type a value directly, or use the up/down stepper to change it by one (it can't go below 0). A Save / Cancel footer appears inside the counter card only when the value differs from what's saved. Cancel reverts it; Save stores the new counter and shows "Business Settings successfully updated." Manage Tax Rates — tap to open a bottom sheet listing your account's tax rates, so you can review and manage them. Note: If the screen fails to load, tap Retry . This is a focused, mobile version of Business Settings — it doesn't include your company name, address, or logo (manage those on the web). Availability Tap Settings > Availability to set the days and hours you're available, plus any exceptions. Work Days — one card per day, Monday through Sunday : Toggle a day on to work that day (a default 8:00 AM–5:00 PM slot is added) or off to remove all its slots. Each slot has a From and To time — tap either to pick a time. Tap + Add Time Slot to add another slot (up to 5 per day ). Tap the X to remove a slot (you can't remove the last one). Exceptions — periods when all your services are unavailable. Tap the + to add one. You can have up to three, one of each type: By Day Range — a start and end date. Turn on Annual Exception to repeat it every year. By Month — pick one or more months (Jan–Dec). By Season — pick Winter, Spring, Summer, and/or Fall. A live summary shows exactly what will be blocked. Tap Add Exception to save it, or the trash icon on a card to remove it. Save your changes: the Reset and Save buttons at the bottom light up only when you have unsaved changes. Reset discards edits; Save shows "Availability successfully updated." Notification Settings Tap Settings > Notifications to control which alerts you get and where. Each notification category has two switches — Email and Mobile (push) — that you toggle independently. The categories are: Financial Jobs Estimates Appointments Timesheets Inventory Team Messages Feedback Tap Save to apply ("Notifications successfully updated"), or Reset to undo pending changes. Both buttons enable only when you've made a change. Note: These switches control Email and Mobile push only; any other channels configured for your account are left as they are.
users-management: User Management Overview This is where you manage everyone who has access to your DHS account — your office staff and your field crews. Each user gets a role that decides what they can reach, and can belong to one or more crews. From this section you can: Add users with their contact details, a role, and a password. Edit anyone's profile, change their role, or update their photo. Disable someone who should no longer get in, and enable them again later. Send a password reset so they can set their own. Search and filter by name, email, or role. Important: users are never deleted, only disabled. Disabling stops someone signing in but keeps everything they did — their jobs, appointments and timesheets stay intact, and their name still shows on the records they worked. Enable them again and they're straight back in. The Users list To open it, go to Menu > Users . The Users list. The tab you are on is named in the card header, with a count. Active and Disabled Two tabs split the list: Active — everyone who can sign in right now — and Disabled , everyone whose access you've turned off. The card header names the tab you're on and counts it. Columns Column What it shows User Their photo and full name. Sortable. Click the name to open their profile. Email Address The address they sign in with. Sortable. Role Their role, as a coloured tag. Sortable. Crew Every crew they belong to. Empty for someone who isn't on one — office staff, usually. Actions Depends on the tab. See below. Row actions On the Active tab: Action What it does Edit Opens their profile. Clicking their name does the same. Disable Asks you to confirm, then takes away their access. On the Disabled tab, Edit stays and Enable takes its place, to give someone their access back. Two things stop a disable, and both are deliberate: Your own row has no disable button at all. You can't lock yourself out. Someone assigned to active jobs can't be disabled — the button is greyed out and reads "Cannot Disable User With Active Job Assignments". Reassign or finish their work first. Search and the role filter The search box in the card header matches names and email addresses. Next to it, Filter opens a panel where you tick the roles you want to see — pick several to combine them, and Reset Filter clears them. Filter by role to see only admins, only crew, or any combination. Sorting and pages Click the User , Email Address , or Role header to sort by it, and again to reverse. The Crew column isn't sortable. The list shows 10 users per page; switch to 20, 50, or 100 at the bottom left. The guided tour The first time you open the list, a short tour points out the Add User button, the tabs, the list, search, and the role filter. Skip dismisses it for good. Roles Every user has exactly one role. It's the single most important field on their profile, because it decides what they see when they sign in. Role Tag Who it's for Owner Grey Whoever created the account. There's normally one, and you can't hand the role out — it isn't offered when you add or edit someone. Admin Green Full run of the platform: users, crews, settings, and the whole business side. The highest role you can give someone. Support Yellow Office and dispatch — scheduling, talking to clients, keeping the day moving, without full admin reach. Crew Member Blue The field: technicians and installers who work jobs. This is what Quick Add gives a new user. Only Owner , Admin and Crew Member users can be put on a crew. Support users don't appear in the crew member picker — they're office staff, not field staff. Adding a user Click Add User . A panel slides in from the right, titled Add New User . Adding a user. The role decides what they see once they sign in. Field Required Notes Profile picture No Upload Image to add a photo, up to 4 MB. It shows up wherever they appear — the users list, crew avatars, job assignments — so it's worth adding. First Name / Last Name Yes Email Address Yes What they sign in with, so it has to be theirs and it has to be unique. If it's already registered you'll be told when you leave the field. Phone Number Yes With a country selector, set to the US by default. Role Yes Admin, Support, or Crew Member. See Roles above. Timezone Yes Theirs, not yours. It's how dates and times are shown to them, which matters for anyone working in another timezone. Description No Notes for your own team: certifications, what they specialise in, what they're responsible for. Set Password / Confirm Yes Their first password, emailed to them. Confirm appears once you start typing. The password It needs at least 10 characters , and among them an uppercase letter , a lowercase letter , a number , and a special character . Rather than inventing one, use the generate button beside the field — it makes a password that already passes — then Copy if you want to pass it on yourself. Either way the password is emailed to the address you entered, so the new user gets it without you having to send anything. Click Add User to finish. Editing a user Click the pencil on their row, or their name. The panel opens as Edit User with everything filled in: photo, name, email, phone, role, timezone, description. Editing a user. The password fields are replaced by Reset Password, which emails them a link. The password fields aren't here — you don't get to see or set someone's password after the fact. Instead there's Reset Password , which emails them a link to choose a new one themselves. That section doesn't appear when you're editing your own profile. To change someone's photo, Upload Image replaces it and the remove button clears it back to the default avatar. Save with Apply Changes . Turning access off and on When someone leaves, or shouldn't be signing in for a while, disable them. Nothing they did is lost. Disabling From the Active tab, click the disable button on their row and confirm. You can also do it from inside their profile: the button sits at the top of the panel and asks you to confirm right there. Disabling asks first. Note the greyed buttons on other rows — those users have active job assignments. They move to the Disabled tab and can't sign in from that moment. Their history stays, and their name keeps showing on the work they did. Remember the two cases that block it: your own account, and anyone with active job assignments. Enabling Switch to the Disabled tab, click enable on their row, and confirm — or open their profile and use the button at the top. They're back on the Active tab and can sign in immediately, with the same password as before. Users added in a hurry Building a crew and the person you need isn't a user yet? Quick Add — from the top bar, or from inside the crew member picker — takes just enough to create them and get you back to what you were doing. Quick Add takes just enough to create someone and get you back to what you were doing. They're created as a Crew Member , and their row carries a marker offering Complete Info until someone fills in the rest: their role if it should be different, their timezone, their phone. The marker clears when you save the full profile. Where users show up Crews — Owner, Admin and Crew Member users can be crew members, and one of them is the crew lead. Appointments and jobs — work is assigned to crews, and their members are who turns up. Someone with active assignments can't be disabled. Timesheets — hours are recorded per user, whether the timer ran or the entry was added by hand. Messaging — users take part in internal team threads and in conversations with clients. Reports — timesheet and performance reporting is broken down by user. crews-management: Crews Management Overview A crew is a team of users who work together. Instead of assigning technicians one by one to every appointment, job, or estimate, you group them into a crew and assign the whole team at once. Each crew has a name, a color that identifies it across the platform, and a crew lead who is the primary point of contact for that team. From this section you can: Create crews with a name, color, description, and members. Edit a crew to change its details, add or remove members, or hand the lead role to someone else. Delete crews you no longer need. Review availability for each crew, and jump to the Availability page to change its schedule. See customer feedback and ratings for each crew. Search and filter crews by name, or by the people on them. Important: a crew can only be deleted if it is not assigned to any job or estimate . While a crew is in use its delete button stays greyed out, and hovering it explains why: "Cannot delete crew assigned to jobs or estimates." The Crews list The Crews list is where you manage every crew. To open it, go to Menu > Crews . The Crews list. Search and the Users filter sit in the card header, next to the crew count. Two things sit above and inside the list: Add Crew — the button at the top right of the page. It opens the create panel. The card header — holds the title with a count of your crews, a search box, and a Users filter. On a phone the layout folds: Add Crew moves to its own strip at the top of the screen and the search box sits below it, full width. Columns Column What it shows Crew The crew's name, with a dot in the crew's color. Click the header to sort the list by name, A–Z or Z–A. Description The crew's description, trimmed to fit the column. Hover it to read the whole thing. Rating The crew's average customer rating, shown as stars out of five. Ratings come from the feedback clients leave on the crew's completed jobs. Members The crew lead first, then up to two more members, then a +N badge for everyone else. Hover the badge to see who it covers. Disabled users are left out. On a narrow screen only the lead's avatar shows and the badge covers the rest of the team. Actions Three buttons per row — see below. Hover the +N badge to see the members it covers. Row actions Action Icon What it does Edit Pencil Opens the crew for editing — details, members, customer feedback, and availability. Clicking the crew's name does the same thing. Availability Clock Takes you to the Availability page with this crew already selected, ready to change its schedule. Delete Trash Asks you to confirm, then deletes the crew. Greyed out while the crew is assigned to jobs or estimates. Sorting Click the Crew column header to sort the list by name, and click it again to reverse the order. The other columns aren't sortable. Pagination The list shows 10 crews per page. Use the picker at the bottom left to switch to 20, 50, or 100, and the controls at the bottom right to move between pages. Changing the search term or the filter takes you back to the first page. When nothing is listed Which message you get depends on why the list is empty: A search with no match tells you which keyword came up empty, so you can try another one. A filter with no match suggests clearing your filters. No crews at all explains what crews are for, with a shortcut to this help article. A search that matches nothing names the keyword you tried. The guided tour The first time you open the Crews list, a short tour walks you through the page: the Add Crew button, the list itself, search, the Users filter, and the row actions. Use Next to step through it, or Skip to dismiss it — you'll then be asked whether you want to skip just this tour or turn tours off everywhere. Once finished or skipped, it doesn't come back. Creating a crew Click Add Crew . A panel slides in from the right, titled Add New Crew . The Add New Crew panel. Name and at least one member are required. Fields Field Required Notes Crew Name Yes What the team is called — "Plumbing Crew", "Emergency Repair Team". Color No The swatch beside the name. Click it and pick from ten colors; the crew starts out blue. This color is how you recognise the crew in lists and on the scheduler. Description No What the crew does, where it works, anything worth noting. Several lines fit. Crew Members Yes At least one person. Pick them from the dropdown; they're listed in the table underneath. Adding members Open the Add Crew Member dropdown and tick everyone who belongs on the crew. The member picker lists the people who can join a crew. Not everyone on your account shows up here. The list holds users with the Owner , Admin , or Crew role — the people who do field work. Support users and clients are never crew members, and anyone whose account is disabled is left out too. If someone you expect is missing, check their role on the Users page. Need someone who isn't a user yet? Use the Quick Add shortcut inside the dropdown to create them without leaving the crew form. The new person is added to your account and put straight onto the crew. Everyone you pick appears in the members table: The members table, with the crew lead selected on the left. Crew Lead — the first person you add becomes the lead. To hand the role to someone else, select their radio button. Remove — the trash button takes someone off the crew. It's disabled on the last remaining member, since a crew can't be empty. Remove the current lead and the next member on the list takes over. Click Add Crew at the bottom of the panel to finish. Editing a crew Click the pencil on the crew's row, or click its name. The panel opens titled Edit Crew , with the same fields you filled in when you created it, plus two sections that only make sense once the crew exists. Editing a crew. Apply Changes stays greyed out until you change something. Members Add and remove members, or move the lead, exactly as you would when creating a crew. If someone's account has been disabled they stay in the table, greyed out and marked (Disabled) , so you can still see who used to be on the team. They can't be made lead, and they don't count towards the members shown in the list. Customer feedback When clients have rated this crew's work, a feedback section shows the average rating and the most recent comment. If there's no feedback yet, the section isn't there at all. Availability Below that is a read-only summary of when the crew works. The crew's schedule at a glance. Days that share the same hours are grouped together. General schedule — the crew's working hours for each day of the week. Consecutive days with the same hours are grouped into one line, and days the crew doesn't work are marked Unavailable . Exceptions — any period the crew is unavailable, whether that's a date range, a whole month, or a season. This part only appears when exceptions exist. To change any of it, click Manage Availability Settings . That takes you to the Availability page with this crew already selected. If nothing has been set up yet, the summary says so. Saving Click Apply Changes . The button stays greyed out until you actually change something, so there's no way to save an untouched form. Cancel closes the panel and keeps the crew as it was. Deleting a crew Click the trash button on the crew's row. Confirm when you're asked whether you're sure. Deleting is permanent. Crews can't be archived or restored. Records that already reference the crew — past jobs, appointments — keep the crew's details. If the crew is assigned to jobs or estimates, the trash button is greyed out and hovering it reads: "Cannot delete crew assigned to jobs or estimates." Reassign the crew on that work first, then delete it. Quick Add When you're in the middle of something else and need a crew immediately, use Quick Add in the top bar and choose Crew . It also turns up wherever you pick a crew — assigning one to an appointment, for instance. Quick Add asks only for a name and members. Everything else can wait. The short form asks only for a crew name and its members ; everything else can wait. As with the full form, the first member you add becomes the lead, and you can create a new user from inside the member dropdown. Once it's saved you're offered a View Crew shortcut that opens the new crew for editing, so you can fill in its color, description, and schedule. Until you do, the crew is flagged as incomplete in the Crews list: a marker next to its name offers Complete Info , which opens the same panel. Saving the crew from the full form clears the marker. Searching and filtering Search matches crew names. Type in the box in the card header and the list narrows on its own after a moment; capitalisation doesn't matter. The Users filter is a multi-select of the people on your account. Pick one or more and you'll see only the crews they belong to — the quickest way to answer "which crews is this person on?". Search and the filter work together, and the crew count in the header always reflects what you're looking at. The Users filter answers "which crews is this person on?". Crews elsewhere in the platform Crews are used throughout DHS: Appointments When you create or edit an appointment you can assign a crew to it, choosing from a dropdown that shows each crew with its color, or quick-adding one that doesn't exist yet. The crew's availability is taken into account when the appointment is scheduled: if it falls outside their hours or during an exception, you're warned. Jobs Crews can be assigned to jobs, and it's these assignments that decide whether a crew can be deleted. The platform can also spot schedule conflicts and warn you before double-booking a crew that's already working during that window. Estimates Estimates can carry a crew too. When an estimate comes from an existing appointment or job, the crew is filled in from that record. Availability Each crew can keep its own schedule — working days, hours, and exceptions — separate from your business hours. Set one up with Manage Availability Settings , in the crew's Availability section. Dashboard and reports Crew data feeds the reporting areas: average customer rating per crew, satisfaction trends, and how complaints are distributed across crews. clients-management: Clients Management Overview A client is a customer you do business with — a homeowner or a company. Every appointment, estimate, job, and invoice belongs to a client, and each client can have as many properties as they own. From this section you can: Add clients with their contact details, first property, and billing address. Invite clients to connect to your account through the client portal, and see who has accepted. Edit a client's contact and billing information. Archive clients you no longer work with, and restore them later. Manage their properties — add, edit, or remove them, and open one on the map. See everything related to a client — appointments, estimates, jobs, and invoices, all in one place. Message them without leaving the client record. Keep files against the client and against each property. Import and export your client list as CSV. Important: clients are never deleted, only archived. Archiving hides a client from your active list while keeping every appointment, estimate, job, and invoice they were part of. You can restore an archived client at any time. The Clients list To open it, go to Menu > Clients . The Clients list. The tabs sit above it; search and Filters live in the card header. Connected, Invites, Archived Three tabs divide your clients by their relationship with you, not by their type: Tab Who's in it Connected The clients you work with — the ones you added yourself, plus the ones who accepted your invitation. This is where you start. Invites Clients you've invited to the portal who haven't accepted yet, and the ones who declined. Archived Clients you've archived. To filter by Residential or Business , use the Filters panel described below — client type is a filter now, not a tab. Columns Column What it shows Client Name The client's avatar and name, with their company underneath when they have one. Sortable. A badge appears here when an invitation is pending or was declined. Type Residential or Business , taken from the client's main property, with a coloured dot. Sortable. Phone The client's phone number. Email The client's email address. Hover to read a long one in full. Address The main property's address, or the billing address if there's no property yet. When the client owns more, a +N badge appears — hover it for the breakdown by type. Tags The tags you've given the client. Actions A button that opens the client, and a three-dot menu. Click anywhere on a row to open that client. Search and Filters The card header holds a search box — it matches names, company names and email addresses, and narrows the list as you type — and a Filters button. All four filters live in one panel, with Reset Filter to clear them. Filter What it narrows to City Clients with a property in the cities you pick. State Clients with a property in the states you pick. Property Type Residential or Business clients. Tags Clients carrying the tags you pick. Filters combine, and they combine with search and with the tab you're on. The number on the Filters button tells you how many are active, so you always know why the list looks short — and Reset Filter at the top of the panel clears them in one go. The three-dot menu Start a Conversation — opens your thread with this client, creating one if you've never spoken. Attachments — the client's files. Archive , or Restore if the client is already archived. On a client who hasn't accepted your invitation yet, these are all greyed out — there's nothing to manage until they accept. Sorting and pages Click the Client Name or Type header to sort by it, and again to reverse. The list shows 10 clients per page; switch to 20, 50, or 100 at the bottom left. Changing a tab, a filter, or the search takes you back to the first page. The guided tour The first time you open the Clients list, a short tour points out the tabs, the Add Client button, search, Filters, and the row actions. Skip dismisses it and it won't come back. Adding a client Click Add Client . A panel slides in from the right with two steps. Step 1 — Client Contact Information Step 1. Name, phone and email are required; the rest is optional. Field Required Notes First Name / Last Name Yes The person you deal with. Phone number Yes With a country selector, set to the US by default. Email Address Yes Has to be a real address, and it's how the client signs in to the portal if you invite them. Company Name No Fill it in for a business client; it shows under their name in the list. Company email / Company phone No The business's own contact details, when they differ from the person's — a main office line, an accounts inbox. Website No Tags No Type a tag and press Enter. Tags are how you filter the list later — trade, territory, priority, whatever suits you. You can also attach files to the client here, before it even exists. If the email already belongs to a client , the panel tells you instead of creating a duplicate. What happens next depends on the situation: if they're already connected to you, you're pointed at the existing record; if they exist in DHS but aren't connected to you, the step is replaced by their details and a Send invite button; and if you've already invited them, you get the option to send the invitation again. That panel is shown under Inviting a client to the portal , below. Step 2 — Property info & Review Step 2 holds the property, the billing address, and a summary to check before saving. The client's first property comes next: its type (Residential or Business), address , city , state , zip code , and optionally a timezone and a photo of the property. A picture helps crews recognise the place when they arrive — up to 4 MB, in JPEG, PNG or WebP. Below that is the billing address . It's set to match the property address, so leave it alone unless invoices go somewhere else — a management company, a head office — in which case turn it off and type the billing address in. At the bottom, a summary of everything you've entered. Check it and click Add Client . You can move between the two steps with Next Step and the back arrow, and Cancel closes the panel without saving. Inviting a client to the portal Clients can have their own portal account, where they see their estimates, jobs and invoices and message you directly. That connection starts with an invitation from you. An invited client sits on the Invites tab, with a badge on their name: Invitation Pending — they haven't answered yet. Invite declined — they said no. The record stays on the Invites tab for reference. Typing an email that already belongs to a DHS client turns the form into an invitation: their details, and Send invite. While an invitation is unanswered you can't act on that client: opening the row shows a read-only summary of their contact details instead of the full record, and the menu actions are greyed out. Once they accept, they move to Connected and everything unlocks. Once a client uses their portal, they own their own details. Their name, phone, email and properties become read-only for you, and the app says so: "This client updates their own details from their portal." You can still archive them, message them, and keep working — you just can't edit information they now maintain themselves. Ask them to change it on their side. The client record Click a client to open their record. Everything about one client: their work in tabs, contact details and the conversation on the right. The header carries the client's name, whether they're Active or Archived , and a three-dot menu with Attachments and Archive or Restore. A Start a Conversation button appears there too, until you've started one — after that, the conversation itself lives in the sidebar. Client Contact Information , on the right, holds their name and type, phone, email and billing address. The pencil in its corner opens the edit panel. Underneath it, three tabs: Chat — the conversation, right there. Client is your thread with them; Team is the internal one about this client, which the client never sees. Notes — anything your crews should know before they arrive: gate codes, a dog, who to ask for on site. Internal too. Attachments — the client's files. services-management: Services Management Overview A service is labour you charge for — an inspection, an install, a repair, a callout. You define it once with its hourly rate, and from then on you pick it when building an appointment, an estimate, a job, or an invoice, instead of retyping the price every time. From this section you can: Add services with a rate, a description, and any documents that go with them. Edit one when your pricing changes. Archive services you no longer offer, and restore them later. Delete an archived service for good, when nothing references it. Decide what clients see — which services appear in your client portal. Search and filter by tag, group, whether it's taxable, and whether clients can see it. Import and export your service list as CSV. Keep attachments — spec sheets, manuals, safety documents. Important: archiving and deleting are different. Archiving takes a service out of the pickers while keeping every record that used it — that's what you want when you stop offering something. Sortable. Rate What you charge per hour. Sortable, so this is how you find your most and least expensive work. Taxable Ticked when the service is included in tax calculations. Client Portal Ticked when clients can see and request it from your portal. Tags The labels you've given it — a trade, a season, a tier. Groups The groups it belongs to, if any. Actions See below. Attachments — its documents. Archive on the Active tab; Restore Service and Delete on the Archived tab. Description No What the service includes, how long it usually takes, anything that saves a phone call later. Tags No Type a tag and press Enter. Tags are what you filter by later, so a little consistency here pays off. Two switches sit below the fields: Taxable — "Include this service in tax calculations when applicable." Turn it on and tax is worked out automatically wherever the service is used. Show on client portal — clients can see this service and request it themselves. Leave it off for anything you'd rather quote by hand. You can attach documents while creating the service — spec sheets, manuals, anything a crew might need on site. Then click Add Service . Editing a service Open the three-dot menu on the row and choose Edit service . Everything is editable except the SKU. Save with Apply Changes . Editing a service. products-management: Products Management Overview A product is something physical you stock, sell, or install — a filter, a thermostat, a length of pipe. Each one carries what it costs you, what you charge for it, and, if you want, how many you have. Add it to an estimate or an invoice and the price and the stock follow. From this section you can: Add products with cost, markup and price, a photo, and where they come from. Track stock — what's on hand, what's already promised, when to reorder. Edit one product, or bulk edit quantities across many. Archive products you no longer carry, and restore them later. Delete an archived product for good, when nothing references it. Search and filter by tag, group, vendor, manufacturer and more. Import and export your catalogue as CSV. Important: archiving and deleting are different. Archiving takes a product out of the pickers while keeping every record that used it. Deleting is permanent, and only possible once nothing references the product. The Products list To open it, go to Menu > Inventory > Products . The Products list. Cost and Item Price are sortable; Markup is not. Active and Archived Two tabs: Active , what you currently carry, and Archived , what you've retired. Archived products don't appear when you're building an estimate or an invoice, but they stay on everything they were already part of. Columns Column What it shows SKU The code that identifies the product. Set once when you create it and fixed from then on. Sortable. Product Its photo, name, and description. Hover the photo to see it bigger — useful when two parts have similar names. Cost What you pay for it. Sortable. Markup % What you add on top. Item Price What the client pays. Sortable. Taxable Ticked when the product is included in tax calculations. In Use Ticked when at least one estimate, job, or invoice references it. This is what decides whether it can be deleted. Tags The labels you've given it. Groups The groups it belongs to, if any. Actions See below. Row actions Each row has an eye that opens View product details — everything about the product, including its stock, read-only — and a three-dot menu with edit, archive or delete, and the rest. Delete is greyed out while anything references the product: "This item can't be deleted because it's linked to existing records." Archive it instead. Search and filters The search box in the card header matches names and SKUs, and Filter opens a panel to narrow by tag, group, and the product's other attributes. Reset Filter clears them. Filters, search, and the tab you're on all work together. Narrowing the catalogue down. Adding a product Click Add Product . A panel opens from the right, titled Add New Product , with everything on one screen — the essentials first, then the details. Cost, markup and item price are linked — fill in two and the third follows. The essentials Field Required Notes Product Image No A photo. Worth adding — it's what someone recognises in a list of similar parts. SKU Yes A code unique to this product. You can't change it afterwards. If the code is already taken you'll be told when you leave the field. Name Yes What it's called on estimates and invoices, so write it the way a client should read it. Description No Size, model, what it fits — whatever stops someone ordering the wrong one. Cost Yes What you pay your supplier. Markup — Your margin, as a percentage. Item Price — What the client pays. Taxable No Include this product in tax calculations. How cost, markup and price fit together These three are linked, so you only ever fill in two: Enter a cost and a markup , and the item price is worked out — cost plus that percentage. Enter a cost and an item price , and the markup is worked out for you. Which way you work depends on how you price. If you apply a standard margin, type the markup and let the price follow. If the price is fixed — by a manufacturer, or because that's what the market bears — type the price and see what margin it actually leaves you. The details Below the essentials sits everything that makes the product orderable and countable. None of it is required, but it's what turns a price list into a working inventory. Field What it's for Unit Of Measure How you count it: each, box, foot, gallon. Vendor / Vendor SKU Who you buy it from, and their code for it — so reordering doesn't mean hunting through catalogues. Manufacturer / Manufacturer Number Who makes it, and the part number. Average Delivery Time (Days) How long it takes to arrive. This is what tells you how early to reorder. Location Where it lives — a van, a shelf, a bay. Color When the same part comes in several. Group Which group it belongs to. Tags Your own labels, for filtering later. Quantity On Hand How many you have right now. Re-Order Quantity The level at which you want to be warned. Disable inventory tracking Turn counting off for this product. See below. Click Add Product to finish. Stock For anything you count, DHS tracks three numbers rather than one: Number What it means Stock Available What you can still promise. Stock Reserved for Estimates Already quoted, not yet committed. Stock Reserved for Jobs Committed to work in progress. The distinction is the point: ten filters on the shelf with eight already promised to jobs is not ten filters you can sell. Products show up as In Stock , Low stock , or Out of stock depending on where they sit against your re-order quantity. Products you don't count Not everything is worth counting — consumables, bulk fittings, anything you simply never run out of. Turn on Disable inventory tracking for those. They keep their price and work normally on estimates and invoices; they just don't carry quantities and won't warn you about stock. Editing a product Open the three-dot menu on the row and choose Edit product . Everything is editable except the SKU. Save with Apply Changes . Editing a product. The SKU is fixed once created. The edit panel also carries Archive (or Delete , for a product already archived), with a confirmation right there. Updating quantities for several products at once After a stock count or a delivery, editing products one at a time is a waste of an afternoon. Select the rows you want, and bulk edit lets you set Quantity On Hand and Re-Order Quantity for all of them together. The panel tells you what it's about to do — how many products are selected, and whether any of them can't be updated. Products with inventory tracking switched off have no quantities to set, so they're left out; if none of your selection is tracked, you're told that instead of the change silently doing nothing. Turn tracking on in each product's edit panel first. Bulk edit says how many products it will touch, and warns when some cannot be. Archiving, restoring, deleting To archive: three-dot menu > Archive > confirm. The product moves to the Archived tab and stops appearing in pickers. Everything that already used it is untouched. You can archive several at once by selecting their rows. Archiving asks first, and leaves every existing record alone. To restore: Archived tab > three-dot menu > Restore . To delete for good: Archived tab > three-dot menu > Delete > confirm. Only available when the In Use column is empty. Importing and exporting Export CSV downloads your catalogue as a spreadsheet — for a price review, a stock count, or sending a vendor your list. Import CSV brings a catalogue in, which is how you avoid typing hundreds of parts by hand. Upload the file, match your columns to the DHS fields, check the preview, and import. Rows that fail validation are reported so you can fix the file and try again. Note: both buttons can be turned off for your account, in which case neither appears. The product picker has a Quick Add shortcut in it: give a SKU, a name and a price, and you're back where you were with the product created. Its row carries a marker until someone fills in the vendor, the unit and the quantities. Note that products are added this way only — from a picker, while you're building something. The Quick Add panel in the top bar covers appointments, clients, jobs, estimates, crews, users, service items, properties and payments, but not products. Where products are used Estimates — quoted parts. Quantities you quote are held as reserved, so a quote can't promise stock twice. Jobs — parts committed to work in progress. Invoices — what the client is billed for, with tax on the products marked taxable. Groups — a set of products and services you add together, instead of picking them one by one. Changing a product's price changes what future records pick up; records already written keep the price they were created with.
