appointments-management: Appointments Management Overview An appointment is a shorter stop: a site visit, a walkthrough, a quote call, a check-in. It's the thing you book before you know what the work will be — and once you do know, it turns into an estimate or a job without being retyped. From this section you can: Book appointments with a client, a property, a crew and a time. Send the details to the client and get them confirmed. Follow them through — en route, arrived, completed, or a no-show. Track time against the visit. Turn one into an estimate, a job, or an invoice , and see everything that came out of it. The Appointments list To open it, go to Menu > Appointments . The Appointments list. Scheduled For is the column you work from. Column What it shows Name What the appointment is for. Sortable. Client Who you're seeing. Scheduled For When. Sortable — the column you work from. Crew Who's going. Status Where it stands. Sortable. Actions Edit, and a three-dot menu. For the same appointments laid out by time, use the Scheduler ; to see where they are, use Map . Narrow by status, crew and date. Statuses Status What it means Draft Being put together, not sent to anyone. Pending Sent to the client, waiting for them to confirm. Confirmed The client has confirmed. En Route The crew is on the way. Arrived They're there. Completed The visit happened. No Show The client wasn't there. Worth recording rather than cancelling — a pattern of no-shows is something you want to be able to see. Canceled It's not happening. Crews move an appointment through En Route, Arrived and Completed from the mobile app, so the office can see the day unfold. Booking an appointment Click Add Appointment . You choose the client and which of their properties , what the visit is called , the crew , and the date and time . Booking a visit. The crew’s availability is respected while you pick. The crew's availability is respected while you pick, so you can't quietly book someone who's already out on a job. If the client isn't in DHS yet, Quick Add is in the picker. Appointments can also be created straight from the Scheduler by picking a slot, which is usually faster when you're booking around existing work. The appointment Click an appointment to open it. The header has its name and status, a Start Timer action, and a three-dot menu. The sidebar keeps the client's phone and email to hand — this is the record you'll have open when you call to confirm. Two tabs: Overview — the appointment itself: the details, the property, and the services planned for the visit. Related Records — everything that came out of it. Sending it to the client Send to Client sends the appointment details out by email or text, with a preview first. The status moves to Pending until they confirm. This is what stops the "was anyone coming today?" call. What comes out of an appointment This is the part of the section that earns its keep. You went to look at the work; now you know what it is. The Related Records tab turns the visit into the next step, and then keeps the trail. From an appointment you can create When An estimate The client wants a price before committing. Everything you gathered on the visit carries over. A job The work is agreed and just needs scheduling. An invoice The visit itself is what you're billing — a callout, an inspection, a diagnostic. Once created, each one is listed on the same tab, so the appointment becomes the thread you can follow from "we went and looked" to "we were paid". Until then the sections say so plainly — nothing has come from this appointment yet. Tracking time on a visit Start Timer records time against the appointment, which matters for visits you bill by the hour and for knowing what unbilled site visits actually cost you. The hours land in Timesheets like any other time. A note on products Appointments carry services , not products — they're visits, not installs. If parts are involved, that's a job, and the appointment is where you create it from. Editing, cancelling, deleting Edit an appointment from its row or from inside it. If the time changes after the client has confirmed, send it again so they know. Cancel when it isn't happening, and mark No Show when the client wasn't there — the distinction is worth keeping, because one is your change and the other is theirs. Delete is available too, but a cancelled appointment is a more honest record than a missing one. Where appointments connect Estimates, jobs and invoices — created from the appointment and listed on its Related Records tab. Clients — every client's record lists their appointments. Crews — assigned to the visit, and their availability is what the picker respects. Scheduler and Map — the same appointments by time and by place. Timesheets — time recorded against the visit. estimates-management: Estimates Management Overview An estimate is what you send a client before the work starts: what you'll do, what it costs, and how long the price holds. When they say yes, you turn it into a job in a couple of clicks — no retyping. From this section you can: Build an estimate from your services and products, with a crew, a property, and a checklist. Send it to the client by email, by text, or both. Track where it stands — waiting for review, approved, changes requested, rejected. Renew one that expired instead of starting again. Convert it to a job once it's approved. Duplicate one as the starting point for the next. Download a PDF , or archive what you no longer need. Set up a recurring estimate for work that repeats. The Estimates list To open it, go to Menu > Estimates . The Estimates list. Expiration Date is the column to watch. Columns Column What it shows Name What the estimate is called. Sortable. Client Who it's for. Date created When you started it. Sortable. Expiration Date How long the price holds. Sortable — this is the column to watch, because an estimate that lapses needs renewing before a client can accept it. Crew The team the work is assigned to. Status Where the estimate stands. Sortable. Total What it adds up to. Sortable, so this is how you find your biggest open quotes. Actions Quick actions for the row. Archived estimates live on their own tab, out of the way but not gone. Statuses Status What it means Draft You're still working on it. Only you can see it, and everything is editable. Ready for Review Sent to the client and waiting on them. Approved They said yes. This is the one you can convert to a job. Changes Requested They want it different. Edit and send it again. Rejected They said no. Expired The validity period ran out. Edit it, then renew it to put it back in front of them. Search and filters The search box in the card header finds estimates by name and client. Filter opens a panel to narrow by status and the estimate's other attributes, so "everything still waiting on a client" is one click away. Filter by status to find everything still waiting on a client. Filter by status to find everything still waiting on a client. Creating an estimate Click Add Estimate . The panel has two steps. Step 1 — the details Who it's for and what it covers: the client and which of their properties , a name for the estimate, the crew who'd do the work, an expiration date , and a checklist if the job has one. Step 1 is who it is for; step 2 is what you are charging. If the client isn't in DHS yet, Quick Add is right there in the picker — you don't have to abandon the estimate to create them first. Step 2 — the line items Now what you're charging for: the services and products that make up the work. Each comes in with its price already set from your catalogue, and you adjust the quantity. If you've set up groups , add one and its whole set of items comes in at once instead of picking them one at a time. From there they're ordinary lines: change a quantity, drop what isn't needed. Save, and the estimate starts as a Draft . The estimate Click an estimate to open it. An estimate open: its details, the services and products, and the bill. The header carries its name and status, and the buttons that matter for where it stands right now — a draft offers Submit estimate , an approved one offers Convert to job , an expired one offers Renew estimate . Behind More Actions : Duplicate , Download Pdf , and Delete . The Overview tab is the estimate itself: The details — title, crew, checklist, and the property, with Show Map to see where it is. Services and Products — the lines, with quantities and prices. Add, change, or remove them here. The bill — the subtotal, tax on whatever is marked taxable, and the total. Notes — internal, for your team. Chat — the conversation with the client about this estimate. Attachments — photos, plans, anything that supports the quote. The client sidebar keeps their phone and email to hand, so you can chase a quote without going to look them up. When an estimate has a recurring schedule, a Recurring Schedule tab appears alongside Overview. Sending an estimate to a client Open the estimate and click Submit estimate . Sending it out. Email, SMS, or both, with a preview of what the client receives. Choose how it goes out — Email , SMS , or both. Email gets a subject and a message; SMS gets a short one. Both come with sensible default wording, so you can send without writing anything. You can personalise the message with placeholders that get filled in for each client, so one piece of wording works for everyone. Message preview shows exactly what they'll receive, per channel, before it goes. Once sent, the estimate moves to Ready for Review and the client can approve it, reject it, or ask for changes from their portal. When a client asks for changes The estimate comes back as Changes Requested . Edit it — adjust lines, quantities, the price — and submit it again. It returns to Ready for Review . When an estimate expires Prices don't hold forever, which is why an estimate has an expiration date. Once it passes, the estimate becomes Expired and the page tells you so, along with the date it lapsed. You don't have to start again: edit the estimate first — this is your chance to update prices that have moved since — then renew it , and it goes back for review with a fresh validity period. Turning an approved estimate into a job This is the point of the whole thing. Once an estimate is Approved , Convert to job carries everything across — client, property, crew, services, products, checklist — so nothing is retyped and nothing is forgotten. jobs-management: Jobs Management Overview A job is work you've committed to: a client, a property, a crew, a date, and the services and products involved. It's where an approved estimate ends up, where time gets recorded, and where the invoice comes from. From this section you can: Create jobs directly, or let them come from an approved estimate. Schedule them to a crew, with a start and end date. Follow them through — en route, arrived, started, paused, completed. Record visits , so a job that takes several trips is tracked trip by trip. Track time against the job, and against each visit. Work a checklist , when the job has one. Send the details to the client , and collect their feedback afterwards. Invoice the work without re-entering a thing. Set up recurring jobs for work that repeats. The Jobs list To open it, go to Menu > Jobs . The Jobs list. Scheduled is the column you live in. Column What it shows Name What the job is called. Sortable. Client Who it's for. Scheduled When it's booked. Sortable — this is the column you live in. Crew Who's doing it. Status Where it stands. Sortable. Total What the work comes to. Actions Edit and delete. Search finds jobs by name and client, and Filter narrows by status, crew and dates. For a calendar view of the same work, use the Scheduler ; for a map of where it all is, use Map . Narrow by status, crew and dates. Statuses Status What it means Draft Being put together. Not committed to anything yet. Pending Sent to the client, waiting for them to confirm. Confirmed The client has confirmed. Scheduled Booked with a crew and a date, ready to go. En Route The crew is travelling. Arrived They're on site. Started Work is under way. Paused Temporarily stopped — waiting on a part, weather, a decision. Completed Finished. This is what makes it invoiceable. Canceled Not happening. Crews move a job through En Route, Arrived, Started and Paused from the mobile app as the day happens, so the office sees where things are without ringing round. Creating a job Click Add Job . Three steps: the details — client, property, crew, services and products, and a checklist if there is one — then the start date , then the end date . Dates the crew isn't available are marked, so you don't double-book them. Creating a job directly. Most arrive from an approved estimate instead. Most jobs don't start here, though. If the work was quoted, open the approved estimate and use Convert to job — everything carries across. The job Click a job to open it. The header carries its name, status and a Start Timer action, plus a three-dot menu with the rest. The sidebar keeps the client's phone and email to hand. Tabs across the top: Tab What's in it Overview The job itself: details, services, products, the bill, and the client's feedback once they've left it. Visits Every trip made for this job, with the time recorded on each. Checklist When the job has one — the steps to work through on site. Recurring Schedule When the job repeats. Invoices Invoices raised from this job. Visits Not every job is one trip. A repair that needs a part ordered is two visits; a big install might be five. Visits is where each one is recorded, so the time and the story of the job stay straight instead of blurring into a single block of hours. Add Visit records one: the date , the user who made it, the time from and to , and a description . Time is split by what it actually was: Work Time — hands on the job. Job Prep Time — getting ready, loading, picking up materials. Office Time — paperwork and admin for this job. En Route — travel. Expand a visit to see its timesheet records, and to edit or delete it. One thing to know: a visit with a running timer can't be deleted — stop the timer first. Tracking time Start Timer on the job records time as it happens, which is more accurate than remembering at the end of the day. Crews normally run it from the mobile app while they work; the office can also add time by hand on a visit. Either way the hours land in Timesheets , against the user and the job, which is what payroll and job profitability are built on. Checklists When a job carries a checklist, the Checklist tab holds the steps. Crews work through it on site and the job records what was done — useful for consistency, and for proving it afterwards. Sending job details to the client Send to Client sends the job's details out by email or text, with a preview of what they'll receive before it goes. That's what moves a job to Pending , waiting on their confirmation. Completing a job Mark the job Completed when the work is done. If the job has a checklist, it needs to be worked through first — that's the point of having one. Once complete, the client can be asked for feedback, which shows on the job's Overview and feeds the crew ratings you see on the Crews list. Invoicing the work Open the Invoices tab and use Add Invoice from Job . The services, products and totals come straight from the job — no retyping, and nothing forgotten in the transfer. The button needs something to bill: "Add at least one service or product before creating an invoice." A job can carry more than one invoice, which is how staged or partial billing works. Recurring jobs Work that repeats — monthly maintenance, seasonal service — can run on a schedule instead of being created by hand each time. The Recurring Schedule tab is where the pattern lives, and it's also where you choose whether a change applies to this occurrence only or to the whole series . Worth being deliberate about, since one of those rewrites every future job. Editing and deleting What you can change depends on where the job is. A draft is fully editable; a job in progress or completed is progressively locked down, so history isn't quietly rewritten after the fact. Delete is available from the row in the list and from inside the job. A job that's been invoiced or has time recorded against it is part of your records — cancelling is usually the honest option rather than deleting. Where jobs connect Estimates — an approved estimate becomes a job with everything carried over, and keeps a link back. Appointments — a visit that turns into real work becomes a job. Invoices — raised from the job, with its services and products. Timesheets — every timer and manual entry lands there. Checklists — attached to the job and worked on site. invoices-management: Invoices Management Overview An invoice is the bill. It comes from the work — usually straight from a completed job — goes out to the client, and then you track it until the money arrives. From this section you can: Raise invoices , from a job or on their own. Send them to the client by email or text. See what's been read — sent, viewed, paid. Record payments , including part payments, with the method and reference. Chase what's late , by due date and balance. Download a PDF for clients who need one. The Invoices list To open it, go to Menu > Invoices . Due date and Total Balance together are the whole of credit control. Column What it shows Number The invoice number. Sortable. Client Who's being billed. Linked to The job or estimate it came from, so you can get back to the work behind the bill. Issue date When it was raised. Due date When payment is expected. Sortable — this is how you find what's overdue. Status Where it stands. Sortable. Total Balance What's still owed. Sortable, so the largest outstanding amounts come to the top. Actions Edit and delete. Sorting by Due date and by Total Balance is the whole of credit control: the first tells you what's late, the second tells you what's worth chasing first. Filter by status to separate what is sent from what is paid. Statuses Status What it means Draft Not sent yet. Fully editable. Sent It's gone to the client. Viewed They've opened it — so "I never got it" has an answer. Payment in Progress A payment is going through the gateway. Paid Settled in full. Creating an invoice Most invoices shouldn't be typed at all. Open the completed job, go to its Invoices tab, and use Add Invoice from Job — the services, products and totals come straight across. To raise one directly, click Add Invoice on the Invoices list and fill in the client, the dates, and the lines. Raising an invoice directly. Billing a finished job is usually faster. A job can carry more than one invoice, which is how you bill in stages: a deposit up front, the balance on completion. The invoice Click an invoice to open it. An invoice open. Job Details holds the work billed; Payments holds the money. The header has its number and status, a Send Invoice button, and a three-dot menu holding Edit invoice , Download Pdf and Delete . Two tabs sit below: Job Details — the work being billed, its services, products and totals — and Payments , which is where money received is recorded. The client sidebar keeps their contact details to hand for when you need to chase. Sending an invoice Send Invoice emails or texts it to the client, with a preview of what they'll receive first. The status moves to Sent , and to Viewed once they open it. Sending an invoice, with a preview first. Recording a payment Open the Payments tab and use Add Payment to record money received: Recording a payment. Less than the total is fine — the balance tracks the rest. Field Notes Amount What was received. Less than the total is fine — that's a part payment, and the balance keeps tracking the rest. Payment Method Cash, Check, Credit Card, Bank Transfer, or Other. Transaction date When it was received, which isn't always today. Payment reference A cheque number, a transfer reference — whatever you'd need to match it to a bank statement later. Status Pending, Completed, Failed, Refunded, or Voided. Notes Anything worth remembering about the payment. Every payment is listed on the Payments tab and can be edited afterwards. The invoice's Balance Due updates as they come in, and once the balance reaches zero the invoice is Paid . That status on the list is why part payments are worth recording as they arrive rather than at the end: an invoice showing a small remaining balance is a very different conversation from one showing the full amount. Editing and deleting A draft invoice is fully editable. Once it's been sent — and especially once a payment is against it — an invoice is a financial record, so what you can change narrows. Correcting a sent invoice usually means issuing a new one rather than quietly rewriting the old. Delete is available from the row in the list and from inside the invoice, but think twice about deleting anything a client has already seen or paid. Edit invoice, Download Pdf and Delete sit behind More Actions. Sharing a PDF Download Pdf gives you the invoice as a document, for clients who file paper or need to pass it to an accounts department. Estimates — an estimate becomes a job, and the job becomes the invoice. The Linked to column keeps the trail. Clients — a client's record lists their invoices, so you can see everything they owe in one place. Services and products — the lines, with tax applied to whatever is marked taxable. timesheets-management: Timesheets Management Overview Timesheets are how you track working hours for your team. Each timesheet belongs to a specific user and a specific date, and contains one or more time entries that record what the person did and for how long. Time entries are categorized by type — whether the person was traveling to a job site (en route), performing work at a job site (job time), or working in the office (office time). Timesheets follow an approval workflow : they start as a Draft , get Submitted by the user for review, and are then either Approved or Rejected by an administrator or owner. This process ensures that hours are reviewed and verified before they are finalized. From this section you can: Create new timesheets for any user and date. Add time entries to track specific blocks of work, travel, or office time. Link and unlink time entries between timesheets. Submit timesheets for approval. Approve or reject timesheets (admins and owners only). Delete timesheets and time entries (with restrictions on approved timesheets). View analytics with summary cards showing total hours, en route time, office time, and job time. Search and filter by date range, user, and status. Important: Once a timesheet is approved , it becomes read-only. You cannot edit, delete, or unlink time entries from an approved timesheet. This protects finalized records from accidental modifications. Timesheets List View The Timesheets List View is the main view for managing all timesheets. To access it, navigate to Menu > Timesheets . Summary Cards At the top of the page, four summary cards show aggregated statistics for the current view. Each card shows a value and a percentage change compared to the previous week (with an up or down arrow indicator): Card Icon What It Shows Total Hours Timer The combined total of all hours across all displayed timesheets. Shows percentage change compared to the previous week. Total En Route Hours Truck The total travel time (en route hours) across all displayed timesheets. Total Office Time Building The total office hours across all displayed timesheets. Total Job Time Wrench The total on-site job hours across all displayed timesheets. Tip: The summary cards update based on your active filters. If you filter by a specific user or date range, the cards show the totals for that filtered view only. Controls and Filters Below the summary cards you will find: A New Timesheet button — click to open the create timesheet form. A Search bar — type a keyword to search across timesheets (with a slight delay for performance). A Date Range filter — select a predefined range or custom date range. Defaults to "All Time." A User filter (hidden for crew members) — a multi-select dropdown to filter timesheets by specific users. Shows up to 100 users. A Status filter — a popover with checkboxes for Draft, Pending, Approved, and Rejected. Shows a badge with the count of selected filters. Includes a "Reset filter" button to clear all selections. Note: Crew members can only see their own timesheets. The User filter is hidden for crew members since they cannot view other people's timesheets. Admins and Owners can see all timesheets across the account. Table Columns Column What It Shows User The user's avatar and full name. Timesheet Date The date the timesheet covers, formatted as short month, day, and year (for example, "Feb 19, 2026"). This column is sortable. Office Time Total office hours for this timesheet, displayed in HH:MM format (for example, "02:30"). Job Time Total on-site job hours for this timesheet, displayed in HH:MM format. En Route Time Total travel hours for this timesheet, displayed in HH:MM format. Status The timesheet's current status as a colored tag. This column is sortable. Actions Edit and Delete buttons (see Row Actions below). Status Tags Status Tag Color Meaning Draft Purple/Indigo background The timesheet is being worked on and has not been submitted for review. Pending Gray background The timesheet has been submitted and is waiting for an admin/owner to review it. Approved Green background The timesheet has been reviewed and approved. It is now read-only. Rejected Red background The timesheet has been reviewed and rejected. The user should make corrections and resubmit. Row Actions Action Icon What It Does Edit Pencil icon Navigates to the timesheet's detail page where you can view and manage all time entries. Delete Trash icon Deletes the timesheet. This button is disabled for approved timesheets — the tooltip reads: "This timesheet has been approved and cannot be deleted." Pagination The list uses server-side pagination with a default page size of 10 timesheets per page. Pagination controls at the bottom let you change pages and adjust the page size. Empty State If no timesheets match your search or filters, the table shows: "No Timesheets Found." Creating a New Timesheet To create a new timesheet: Step 1: Click the New Timesheet button at the top of the Timesheets List View. A modal dialog opens. Step 2: Fill in the timesheet details. Error if empty: "Date is required." User Yes The user this timesheet belongs to. Select from a dropdown of all users. Supports Quick Add to create new users inline. Error if empty: "User is required." Note: Crew members can only create timesheets for themselves. The User dropdown is disabled for crew members with the helper text: "Crew members can only create their own timesheets." Step 3: Click Add Timesheet to create the timesheet. The button shows "Saving..." while processing. On success: "Timesheet successfully created." On failure: "Failed to create a timesheet." After creation, you will be taken to the timesheet's detail page where you can start adding time entries. Timesheet Detail Page The detail page is where you manage a single timesheet and all its time entries. To access it, click the Edit button on any timesheet row, or navigate directly after creating a new timesheet. Page Header At the top of the detail page you will see: A Back button (chevron icon) — navigates back to the Timesheets List View. The timesheet description or the user's full name as the page title. The user's avatar and name with their crew affiliation. The status — displayed as a dropdown for admins/owners (who can change it directly) or as a read-only label for crew members. Time Entries Section Below the overview, the time entries are organized into two tabs: Tab What It Shows Linked Entries Time entries that are linked to this specific timesheet. These are the entries that count toward this timesheet's totals. Unlinked Entries Time entries that exist but are not linked to any timesheet. You can link them to this timesheet or to a different one. This tab is hidden when the timesheet is Approved. Above the entries table you will find: A Search bar to filter entries. A Date Range filter to narrow entries by date. An Activity filter to show only specific entry types (All Activity, En Route, Work Time, Office Time). An Add Time button (plus icon) to create a new time entry. An Import Time button (download icon) to import entries from jobs. A confirmation dialog appears first. Adding a Time Entry Time entries are the individual blocks of work that make up a timesheet. To add a time entry: Step 1: On the timesheet detail page, click the Add Time button (plus icon). The Add Time modal opens. Step 2: Fill in the entry details. Add Time Entry Form Fields Field Required Description Date Yes The date this work was performed. Cannot be a future date. Error if empty: "Date is required." Job Conditional The job associated with this entry. Required for En Route and Work Time entries. Not required for Office Time entries (since office work is not tied to a specific job). Select from a dropdown of all jobs. Supports Quick Add to create a new job inline. Error: "Job is required for this time type." Time Type Yes Select the type of work being recorded. Three options displayed as tab-like buttons: En Route (traveling to a job), Work Time (working on a job site), or Office Time (working in the office). From Yes The start time of the work period. To Yes The end time of the work period. Must be after the From time. Error if empty: "To time is required." Error if before From: "To time must be after from time." Editing a Time Entry Click the Edit (pencil icon) on any time entry to open the same Add Time modal pre-filled with the entry's current data. Modify any field and click Save to update it. On success: "Time entry successfully updated." Note: You cannot edit time entries on an approved timesheet. The edit button is disabled for approved entries. Linking and Unlinking Time Entries Time entries can exist independently (unlinked) or be associated with a specific timesheet (linked). This flexibility allows you to create time entries first and organize them into timesheets later. Linking an Unlinked Entry Go to the timesheet detail page and switch to the Unlinked Entries tab. Click the Link icon on the entry you want to add. A popover appears with two options: Link — Immediately links the entry to the current timesheet. Select Another — Opens a modal where you can choose an existing timesheet or create a new one to link the entry to. On success: "Time entry successfully linked." Link Entry Modal (Select Another) When you click Select Another , a modal opens with two options: Option What It Does Existing Timesheet Search for and select an existing timesheet from a dropdown. Shows timesheets as "User Name - Date" format. Create New Timesheet Create a new timesheet on the spot by selecting a date and user, then link the entry to it. Unlinking a Linked Entry On the Linked Entries tab, click the Unlink icon on the entry. A confirmation dialog appears with the title Unlink Time Entry and a confirmation message. Click Unlink to confirm, or Cancel to go back. On success: "Time entry successfully unlinked." The entry moves to the Unlinked Entries tab. Warning: You cannot unlink entries from an approved timesheet. The unlink button is disabled for approved timesheets. Timesheet Approval Workflow Timesheets follow a status-based workflow that ensures hours are reviewed before they are finalized. The flow works as follows: Status Flow Draft → (Submit) → Pending → (Approve) → Approved Pending → (Reject) → Rejected Pending → (Withdraw) → Draft Available Actions by Status and Role Status Who Available Actions Draft Timesheet owner Submit Timesheet — Submits for review (status changes to Pending). Pending Timesheet owner Change to Draft — Withdraws the submission (status changes back to Draft). Pending Admin or Owner Approve Timesheet (green button) — Approves the timesheet (status changes to Approved). Reject Timesheet (red button) — Rejects the timesheet (status changes to Rejected). Approved Everyone No actions available. The timesheet is finalized and read-only. Rejected Timesheet owner The user should correct the timesheet and resubmit. Note: Admins and Owners can also change the status directly using a status dropdown in the detail page header, without using the action buttons. Crew members see a read-only status label instead of the dropdown. A confirmation dialog appears. On success: "Timesheet successfully deleted." On failure: "Failed to delete timesheet." Warning: You cannot delete a timesheet that has been Approved . The delete button is disabled and the tooltip reads: "This timesheet has been approved and cannot be deleted." The confirmation dialog title depends on the context: For unlinked entries: Title is "Permanently Delete Time Entry" with a message explaining the entry will be permanently removed. For linked entries: Title is "Delete Time Entry" with a message explaining the entry will be removed from the timesheet. On success: "Time entry successfully deleted." On failure: "Failed to delete time entry." When you select a job for a time entry (En Route or Work Time type), the entry becomes associated with that job's record. Job names appear in the time entry table's Job column. Users and Crews Each timesheet belongs to a specific user. The timesheet detail page shows the user's crew affiliation. When viewing crew-related timesheets, crew names appear with their assigned color indicators. Reports offer additional breakdowns by employee, date range, job, and client, and support PDF generation for printing or sharing. settings-configuration: Settings & Configuration Overview The Settings section is your central hub for configuring every aspect of your DHS account. It controls your company information, user profile, availability, notifications, business rules, payment processing, and more. To access Settings, navigate to Menu > Settings . The Settings page uses a sidebar + content layout: a navigation sidebar on the left lists all available sections, and the main content area on the right displays the selected section's form. The Settings sidebar includes the following sections: Section Description Account Company information, client contact details, and billing address. Profile Your personal information, password, language, and profile picture. Availability Service availability schedule by day-of-week, exception dates, and seasonal exceptions. Dashboard Dashboard display preferences such as list limits and upcoming jobs window. Notifications Notification channel preferences (Email, SMS, Push, Desktop) per category. Business Counter settings, payment disclaimers, Zelle payment options, crew settings, privacy, and tax rates. Timesheet Settings Automatic timesheet linking configuration (account-level and personal override). Accept Payments Stripe Connect integration for accepting credit card payments from clients. Note: Every settings section has a Save button and a Reset button. Changes are not saved until you click Save. The Reset button reverts all fields to their last saved values. 1. Account Settings The Account section manages your company's core information. This is the default section shown when you open Settings. 1.1 Company Information The top of the page shows a profile banner with your company's initial and name. Below it is the Company Information form: Field Required Description Company Name Yes Your business name as it appears throughout the system. Must be 2–100 characters. Email Yes The primary email address for your company account. Must be unique across the system (validated on blur). Maximum 254 characters. Website No Your company website URL. Accepts URLs with or without the https:// prefix. Maximum 255 characters. Timezone Yes Your business timezone. Select from over 100 timezone options. This affects how dates and times are displayed throughout the platform. 1.2 Client Information Optional contact information that can be displayed to your clients: Field Required Description Client Phone No A phone number your clients can use to reach you. Must be in valid phone format if provided. Client Email No An email address your clients can use to contact you. Validated for proper email format. 1.3 Billing Information Your company's billing address, used on invoices and financial documents. checklists-management: Checklists Management [h] [i] Overview The Checklists Management section is where you create and manage reusable checklist templates for your business. Checklists help ensure that jobs are completed thoroughly by defining a set of items that must be reviewed or verified before a job can be marked as complete. Checklists work as templates — you create a checklist once, and then assign it to as many jobs or estimates as needed. Each job gets its own copy of the checklist, so changes made during a job do not affect the original template. From this section you can: Create new checklist templates with a title, description, and a set of items to verify. Edit existing checklists to add, remove, or reorder items. Duplicate an existing checklist to use it as a starting point for a new one. Archive checklists you no longer need (without losing historical data). Restore archived checklists if you need them again. Permanently delete archived checklists that are no longer needed. Search to quickly find a specific checklist. Important: A checklist can only be permanently deleted if it is not currently assigned to any job. If a checklist is in use, you must first remove it from all associated jobs before deletion is possible. Checklists List View The Checklists List View is the main view for managing all your checklist templates. To access it, navigate to Menu > Checklists . When you open the Checklists List View, you will see a table listing all your active checklists. Each row represents one checklist and displays the following information: Column What It Means Date Created The date the checklist was originally created (e.g., "Jan 1, 2026"). Title The name of the checklist, along with its description (if one was provided). The description is shown as smaller text below the name. Options Quick-action buttons to edit, duplicate, or archive/delete the checklist. Clicking anywhere on a row will open that checklist for viewing and editing its items. Active vs. Archived Checklists At the top of the list you will see two tabs: Active — Shows all checklists that are currently available for use. This is the default view. Active checklists can be assigned to new jobs and estimates. Archived — Shows checklists that have been archived (temporarily disabled). Archived checklists do not appear in the dropdown when creating or editing jobs, but any jobs that already have them assigned will continue to work normally. Sorting the List You can sort the checklists by clicking on the column headers for Date Created or Title . Click once to sort in ascending order, and click again to sort in descending order. Searching Use the search bar to the right of the tabs to find checklists by name or description. Type your search term and the results will update automatically. 1. Creating a New Checklist To create a new checklist template, follow these steps: Step 1: Open the New Checklist Form Click the "New Checklist" button (blue) located in the top-right corner of the Checklists List View. A panel will slide open from the right side of the screen. Tip: If the list is empty (no checklists have been created yet), you will see a "Create Your First Checklist" button in the center of the page. Step 2: Enter the Checklist Details Field Required? Description Checklist Title Yes Enter a clear, descriptive name for the checklist (e.g., "HVAC Installation Final Inspection" or "Plumbing Rough-In Checklist"). Maximum 512 characters. Description No Optionally, provide additional context about when or how this checklist should be used. Maximum 512 characters. Step 3: Add Checklist Items Below the title and description, you will see the Checklist Items section. This is where you define the individual tasks or verification points that make up the checklist. To add an item: Type the item title in the text field (e.g., "Verify all connections are sealed"). Press Enter or click the checkmark button to add the item. Repeat for each item you want to include. For each item, you can also check the "Description Required" checkbox. When this is checked, the person completing the job will be required to write a description for that item before the job can be marked as complete. This is useful for items that need documented evidence or notes (e.g., "Record the serial number of the installed unit"). After adding items, they will appear in a list below. You can: Edit an item by clicking the pencil icon next to it. Remove an item by clicking the trash icon next to it. Note: You must add at least one item before you can save the checklist. The "Add New Checklist" button will remain disabled until at least one item has been added. Step 4: Save the Checklist Once you have entered the title and added your items, click the "Add New Checklist" button at the bottom of the panel. You will see a brief "Creating Checklist..." overlay, and once the checklist is created successfully, a confirmation message will appear: "Checklist Successfully Created" . The new checklist will now appear in your Checklists List View and be available for assignment to jobs and estimates. 2. Viewing and Managing Checklist Items To view or edit the items in an existing checklist, click on any checklist row in the Checklists List View. This will open the Checklist Detail page. What You See The detail page shows: The checklist name at the top, with a pencil icon to edit the name and description. A status badge showing whether the checklist is "Active" or "Archived". A "New Item" button to add more items. A table of all checklist items with the following columns: Column What It Means Drag Handle Grip dots on the left side of each row. Click and drag to reorder items (see below). Title The name/description of the checklist item. Description Required A toggle indicator. Blue (filled) means a description is required when completing this item. Gray (hollow) means it is optional. You can click this toggle to change the setting directly from the table. Edit Pencil icon to open the item for editing. Delete Trash icon to remove the item from the checklist. Adding a New Item Click the "New Item" button at the top of the detail page. A dialog will appear with two fields: Title (required) — Enter the item name. Maximum 512 characters. Description Required (optional) — Check this box if a description must be provided when completing this item. Click "Add Item" to save, or "Cancel" to go back. A success message will appear: "Checklist Entry Successfully Created" . Editing an Item Click the pencil icon next to the item you want to edit. A dialog will appear pre-filled with the item's current title and description required setting. Make your changes and click "Apply Changes" , or click "Cancel" to discard. A success message will appear: "Checklist Entry Successfully Updated" . Reordering Items (Drag and Drop) You can change the order in which items appear by dragging and dropping them: Click and hold the drag handle (grip dots) on the left side of the item row. Drag the item up or down to the desired position. Release to drop it in place. The new order is saved automatically. The items will appear in this order wherever the checklist is used (in jobs and when completing jobs). Deleting an Item Click the trash icon next to the item you want to remove. A confirmation dialog will appear: "Are you sure you want to delete [Item Title]?" Click "Delete" to confirm, or "Cancel" to go back. A success message will appear: "Checklist Entry Successfully Deleted" . Note: You cannot delete the last item in a checklist. Every checklist must have at least one item. If you try to delete the last remaining item, the delete button will be disabled with a tooltip: "Cannot delete last item." 3. Editing a Checklist's Name and Description To change the name or description of a checklist (not its items): Open the checklist detail page by clicking on it in the Checklists List View. Click the pencil icon next to the checklist name at the top of the page. A panel will slide open with two editable fields: Checklist Title (required) — Maximum 512 characters. Description (optional) — Maximum 512 characters. Make your changes and click "Apply Changes" . A success message will appear: "Checklist Successfully Updated" . Tip: You can also access the edit panel by clicking the pencil icon in the Actions column on the Checklists List View. 4. Duplicating a Checklist If you want to create a new checklist that is similar to an existing one, you can duplicate it instead of starting from scratch: On the Checklists List View (Active tab), find the checklist you want to duplicate. Click the duplicate icon (copy icon) in the Options column. A confirmation dialog will appear: "Are you sure you want to duplicate [Checklist Name]?" Click "Duplicate" to confirm. A success message will appear: "Checklist Successfully Duplicated" . The duplicated checklist will appear in the list as a new, independent copy. You can then edit its name, description, and items without affecting the original. 5. Archiving Checklists Archiving is a safe way to disable a checklist without permanently deleting it. Archived checklists: Do not appear in the dropdown when creating or editing jobs and estimates. Are preserved in historical records — any existing jobs that have this checklist assigned will continue to work normally. Can be restored at any time if you need the checklist again. How to Archive a Checklist On the Checklists List View (Active tab), locate the checklist you want to archive. Click the archive icon in the Options column. A confirmation dialog will appear: "Are you sure you want to archive [Checklist Name]?" Click "Archive" to confirm, or "Cancel" to go back. You will see an "Updating Checklist..." overlay, followed by a success message: "Checklist Successfully Archived" . The checklist will be removed from the Active tab and moved to the Archived tab. 5.1 Restoring an Archived Checklist If you need to bring an archived checklist back into active use: Switch to the Archived tab on the Checklists List View. Find the checklist you want to restore. Click the restore icon (undo icon) in the Options column. A confirmation popover will appear: "Do you want to restore this checklist?" Click "Restore" to confirm. A success message will appear: "Checklist Successfully Restored" . The checklist will be moved back to the Active tab and will once again appear in the dropdown when creating or editing jobs. 5.2 Permanently Deleting a Checklist Permanent deletion is only available for archived checklists and only when the checklist is not in use (not assigned to any job). Switch to the Archived tab on the Checklists List View. Find the checklist you want to permanently delete. Click the delete icon (trash icon) in the Options column. If the delete icon is grayed out (disabled), it means the checklist is still assigned to at least one job. You will see a tooltip: "Checklist cannot be deleted while in use." A confirmation dialog will appear: "Are you sure you want to delete [Checklist Name]?" Click "Delete" to confirm, or "Cancel" to go back. You will see a "Deleting Checklist..." overlay, followed by a success message: "Checklist Successfully Deleted" . Warning: Permanent deletion cannot be undone. Once a checklist is deleted, it is removed from the system permanently. If you are unsure, keep the checklist archived instead. 6. How Checklists Are Used Across the Platform Checklists are primarily used in Jobs and Estimates . When you assign a checklist to a job, the job gets its own independent copy of the checklist — so any changes made to items during the job (adding entries, filling in descriptions) do not affect the original template. Assigning a Checklist to a Job When creating or editing a job, you will see a "Checklist (Optional)" dropdown in the Job Details step. This dropdown lists all your active checklists (archived checklists are not shown). Select a checklist to assign it to the job. Once a checklist is assigned to a job: A "Checklist" tab appears on the job detail page. The Checklist tab shows all the items from the template, displayed in order. You can expand each item by clicking the chevron to enter a description or notes for that item. If an item has "Description Required" enabled, it will be marked with an asterisk (*), and a description must be provided before the job can be completed. You can also add new items directly to the job's checklist — these additions only affect the job, not the original template. You can delete items from the job's checklist — again, this only affects the job copy. Completing a Job with a Checklist When you attempt to mark a job as complete, and the job has a checklist assigned: A completion modal will appear showing all checklist items with checkboxes. You must check every item to confirm it has been completed or verified. For items marked as "Description Required", a description text field will appear when you check the item. You must fill in the description before proceeding. The "Complete Job" button will remain disabled until all items are checked and all required descriptions are filled in. This ensures that no job is marked as complete without first verifying all items on the checklist. Note: If a job does not have a checklist assigned, the completion modal will simply ask: "Are you sure you want to complete this job?" without any checklist review. Assigning a Checklist to an Estimate Similar to jobs, you can assign a checklist to an estimate using the "Checklist (Optional)" dropdown on the Estimate Details step. When the estimate is later converted to a job, the checklist assignment carries over. Understanding Checklist Items Each item in a checklist is simple by design. An item has just two properties: Property What It Means Title A short description of what needs to be checked or verified (e.g., "Test water pressure at all fixtures"). Maximum 512 characters. Description Required When enabled, the person completing the job must write a description or notes for this item (e.g., "Record the pressure reading in PSI"). When disabled, the item only needs to be checked off. This simplicity makes checklists easy to create and fast to complete in the field, while the "Description Required" option provides accountability for items that need documented verification. whatsapp-ai: WhatsApp AI Assistant Overview The WhatsApp AI Assistant is a conversational AI built right into WhatsApp that lets you manage your entire DHS business from your phone — using simple text messages or voice memos. Instead of switching between apps, you can search for clients, create appointments, send invoices, check your schedule, and much more, all from a WhatsApp chat. With the WhatsApp AI Assistant you can: Search and look up clients, jobs, estimates, invoices, crews, and more Create new records like appointments, clients, jobs, estimates, and invoices Update and manage existing records — change statuses, reschedule, edit fields Track time — clock in, clock out, and review timesheets Communicate — send messages and notifications to your team or clients Get reports — daily briefings, schedule summaries, and business reports Use utilities — check the weather, get directions, run quick calculations The assistant supports over 103 tools and works in both English and Spanish . You can type your requests in natural, everyday language — no special commands to memorize. Getting Started Linking Your WhatsApp Number Before you can use the WhatsApp AI Assistant, you need to link your WhatsApp phone number to your DHS account. Here is how: Open the DHS app on your phone or desktop. Go to Settings and select WhatsApp Integration . Enter the phone number associated with your WhatsApp account. Tap Link Number . You will receive a verification code via WhatsApp. Enter the verification code in the DHS app to confirm the link. Once verified, you can start messaging the DHS AI Assistant directly on WhatsApp. Authentication and Security Your WhatsApp AI session is protected by multiple layers of security: Twilio Verification — Your phone number is verified through Twilio to confirm your identity. Session Lock — After a period of inactivity, your session is automatically locked. To unlock it, you will receive a verification email with a secure link. Email Verification — When your session locks, simply check your email, click the verification link, and your WhatsApp session will unlock automatically. If someone else tries to message the assistant from an unlinked number, they will not be able to access any account data. What You Can Do The WhatsApp AI Assistant gives you access to over 103 tools organized into the categories below. You do not need to memorize tool names — just describe what you need in plain language and the assistant will figure out the right action. Search and Look Up Quickly find any record in your DHS system by asking the assistant. vendors-manufacturers-groups: Vendors, Manufacturers & Groups Overview Three short lists sit alongside your catalogue and make it easier to work with: Vendors — who you buy from. Attach one to a product and reordering stops being a search through old invoices. Manufacturers — who makes it. This is what answers a warranty call two years after the install. Groups — sets of items that always go out together, so you add the whole set in one step instead of picking parts one by one. All three live under Menu > Inventory , and all three work the same way: a list, a panel to add or edit, a read-only view, and a delete. None of them can be archived — unlike products and services, these are either there or they aren't. Vendors Go to Menu > Inventory > Vendors . The list shows each vendor's Name , Company , Phone , Email and Address . Each row has buttons to view the vendor's details, edit them, or delete the vendor. Adding a vendor Click Add Vendor and fill in what you know: Field Notes Name Your contact there — the person who actually answers. Position Their role, when it helps to know who you're calling. Company Name The business you're buying from. Email Address Where purchase orders and questions go. Website Their catalogue or ordering site. City / State / Zipcode Where they are, which matters when delivery time does. Connecting a vendor to a product A vendor on its own does nothing much. The value comes from the link: open a product, and set its Vendor and Vendor SKU — their code for the part, which is rarely yours. Combined with Average Delivery Time on the product, you know who to call, what to ask for, and how early to ask. Manufacturers Go to Menu > Inventory > Manufacturers . The list shows Company Name , Contact Name , Phone , Email and Address , with the same view, edit and delete buttons on each row. Adding a manufacturer Click Add Manufacturer : Field Notes Company Name The brand. Contact Person Name A rep, if you have one. Email Address General contact. Support Email Address Kept separately on purpose — warranty and technical questions rarely go to the same inbox as sales, and this is the one you'll want when something fails on site. Website Where the spec sheets and manuals live. City / State / Zipcode Vendor or manufacturer? They're not the same thing and a product can have both. The manufacturer made the part; the vendor sold it to you. You might buy the same brand from three different suppliers, or one supplier might carry a dozen brands. On the product you record the manufacturer's part number and the vendor's SKU side by side — one to identify the part, the other to reorder it. Groups Go to Menu > Inventory > Groups . A group is a bundle: the items that always go out together for a particular kind of work. A furnace replacement that's always the same unit, the same filter, the same thermostat and four hours of labour. Instead of adding each line by hand every time, you add the group. The list shows the group's Group Code , Group Name , Description and SKU , and each row lets you view its details, edit it, or delete it. Creating a group Click Add Group : Field Notes Group Code A short code unique to this group. You'll be told if it's already taken. Group Name What the bundle is for, in words someone else would recognise: "Furnace Replacement — Standard". Description What's in it and when to use it. SKU The items that make up the group. Using a group When you're building an estimate or an invoice, add the group and its items come in as individual lines — each with its own price, quantity, and tax setting. From that point they behave like any other line: change a quantity, drop one that isn't needed, leave the rest. That's the important part: a group is a shortcut for adding items, not a link that stays . Editing the group later doesn't rewrite estimates you've already sent, and removing a line from an estimate doesn't touch the group. Groups save you the typing; the record is yours to adjust. Products and services can also be filtered by group on their own lists, which is a quick way to see everything that belongs to one kind of job. Deleting any of the three Use the delete button on the row and confirm.
